description: A case in which the Court held that, according to trust law, the fiduciary duty includes a continuing duty to monitor investments, and that a breach of that duty within six years of the filing of a lawsuit under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act is sufficient to allow the case to proceed.

name: Alabama Department of Revenue v. CSX Transportation, Inc.
question:
Does a state violate the Railroad Revitalization and Regulatory Reform Act of 1974 when it requires rail carriers to pay a sales-and-use tax but exempts the railroad's competitors?

In resolving such a claim, should a court consider other aspects of the state's tax scheme rather than focusing solely on the challenged provision?
description: A case in which the Court held that, in evaluating whether a tax is discriminatory under the Railroad Revitalization and Regulatory Reform Act of 1974, courts may consider competitors an appropriate comparison class and must examine the tax code as a whole rather than solely the challenged provision.

name: Heien v. North Carolina
question: Does a police officer's mistake of law provide the individualized reasonable suspicion that the Fourth Amendment requires to justify a traffic stop?
description: A case in which the Court decided that search and seizures are acceptable if a police officer made a reasonable factual or legal mistake.

name: Zivotofsky v. Kerry
question: Does a federal statute that directs the Secretary of State to record the birthplace of an American citizen born in Jerusalem as "Israel," if requested to do so, impermissibly infringe on the President's power to recognize foreign states?
description: A case in which the Court held that a federal statute directing the Secretary of State to record the birthplace of a citizen born in Jerusalem as “Israel” if requested to do so impermissibly infringed on the President’s power to recognize foreign states.

name: Holt v. Hobbs
question: Does the Arkansas Department of Corrections grooming policy violate the Religious Land Use and Institutionalized Persons Act by preventing Holt from growing a one-half-inch beard in accordance with his religious beliefs?
description: A case in which the Court held that the Department of Corrections' grooming policy violated an inmate's right to religious exercise.

name: Jesinoski v. Countrywide Home Loans, Inc.
question: Does the Truth in Lending Act allow a borrower to rescind a loan by notifying the creditor within the three-year time frame, even though a lawsuit has not yet been filed?
description: A case in which the Court ruled that the Truth in Lending Act allows a borrower to rescind a loan by notifying the creditor within the three-year time frame, even though a lawsuit has not yet been filed.

name: Johnson v. United States
question: Is the definition of "violent felony" in the Armed Career Criminal Act unconstitutionally vague?
description: A case in which the Court determined that the residual clause of the Armed Criminal Career Act is unconstitutionally vague.

name: Dart Cherokee Basin Operating Company LLC v. Owens
question: Is a defendant seeking removal of a case to federal court required to provide evidence supporting federal jurisdiction in the notice of removal?
description: A case in which the Court ruled that a defendant seeking removal of a case to federal court is not required to provide evidence supporting federal jurisdiction in the notice of removal.

name: Kimble v. Marvel
question: Should the decision in Brulotte v. Thys Co, which held that a patentee cannot continue to receive royalty payments after the patent has expired, be overturned?
description: A case in which the Court determined that its earlier decision in Brulotte v. Thys Co., which held that a patentee cannot continue to receive royalties after the expiration of the patent, should be upheld.

name: Jennings v. Stephens
question: Did the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit err in holding that that a federal habeas petitioner who prevailed in district court must file a separate certificate of appealability to respond to the state's appeal?
description: A case in which the Court held that a federal habeas petitioner who prevailed in district court does not need to file a separate certificate of appealability to respond to the state's appeal.

name: Yates v. United States
question: Are fish considered "tangible objects" for the purpose of the statute that makes it a crime to destroy or conceal tangible objects to impede a governmental investigation, even though the term is undefined and exists in a statute that largely refers to record-keeping documents?
description: A case in which the Court ruled that a “tangible item” as defined by Section 1519 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act is one used to record or preserve information.

name: Teva Pharmaceuticals USA, Inc. v. Sandoz, Inc.
question: Can a district court's finding of fact in the construction of a patent claim be reviewed de novo, as though for the first time, which the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit requires and did in this case?
description: A case in which the Court ruled that a federal appellate court can only overturn a district court’s finding of fact if those findings were determined to be “clearly erroneous.”

name: Department of Homeland Security v. MacLean
question: Does the Whistleblower Protection Act bar an agency from taking enforcement action against an employee who intentionally discloses sensitive security information?
description: A case in which the Court ruled that the Whistleblower Protection Act bars an agency from taking enforcement action against employees who intentionally disclose sensitive security information.

name: Alabama Legislative Black Caucus v. Alabama
question: Did the district court apply the correct law when evaluating whether Alabama’s 2012 redistricting violated the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment and the Voting Rights Act of 1965?
description: A case in which the Court held that states may not substitute their own extraneous goals for the traditional goals of the Voting Rights Act of 1965 when redrawing electoral districts.

name: Commil USA, LLC v. Cisco Systems, Inc.
question: Is a good-faith belief that a patent is invalid a defense to a claim of induced infringement?
description: A case in which the Court decided that a good-faith belief that a patent is invalid is not a defense to a claim of induced infringement.

name: Whitfield v. United States
question: Does the forced accompaniment offense require proof of more than minimum movement on the part of the victim?
description: A case in which the Court held that forced accompaniment during the commission of a crime occurs when a person requires another to “go with” him, even when that movement occurs over a short distance.

name: Wellness International Network v. Sharif
question:
(1) Does the presence of a subsidiary state law issue to determine whether property in a debtor's possession is part of the bankruptcy estate mean that the issue does not stem from the bankruptcy itself and therefore that the bankruptcy court does not have jurisdiction to issue a final ruling?

(2) Can bankruptcy courts exercise the judicial power of the United States by litigant consent, and if so, can that consent be implied?
description: A case in which the Court held that claims that would normally be adjudicated by an Article III court can be adjudicated in a non-Article III court as long as the parties knowingly and voluntarily consent.

name: Lopez v. Smith
question: Did the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit properly apply its own precedent in determining that Smith's habeas petition should be granted?
description: A case in which the Court ruled that the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit improperly applied its own precedent to create a habeas relief rule more specific than the rule established by Supreme Court decision.

name: T-Mobile South, LLC v. City of Roswell, Georgia
question: Does a document stating that an application has been denied without providing reasons for the denial comply with the "in writing" requirement of the Telecommunications Act?
description: A case in which the Court held that the Telecommunications Act of 1996 does not require localities to provide reasons for their denial of construction applications in the written denial notification as long as the reasons appear in some other sufficiently clear written record.

name: Elonis v. United States
question: Does a conviction of threatening another person under 18 U. S. C. §875(c) require proof of the defendant's subjective intent to threaten?
description: A case in which the Court found that in order to violate the transmission of threats provision, the threat requires both an objective and subjective intent.

name: Rodriguez v. United States
question: Is the use of a K-9 unit, after the conclusion of a traffic stop and without reasonable suspicion of criminal activity, a violation of the Fourth Amendment prohibition on unreasonable search and seizures?
description: A case in which the Court held that the use of a K-9 unit at the conclusion of an otherwise lawful traffic stop constituted an unreasonable search and seizure in violation of the Fourth Amendment.

name: Baker Botts, LLP v. ASARCO, LLC
question: Does the Bankruptcy Code allow a firm to be awarded damages for defending a challenge to a fee request?
description: A case in which the Court held that the Bankruptcy Code does not provide an explicit statutory exception to the American rule of attorney fees—that each litigant pays for his own attorney’s fees.

name: King v. Burwell
question: Did the Internal Revenue Service permissibly create a regulation that extended the tax credits the Affordable Care Act authorized to federal exchanges as well as those created by the states?
description: A case in which the Court determined that the plain language of the Affordable Care Act extended tax credits to federally-created exchanges as well as those the states created.

name: Bullard v. Blue Hills Bank, fka Hyde Park Savings
question: Is an order denying confirmation of a bankruptcy plan appealable?
description: A case in which the Court held that a bankruptcy court’s order denying confirmation of a repayment plan is not a final order for the purpose of immediate appeal.

name: Walker v. Texas Division, Sons of Confederate Veterans, Inc.
question:
1. Do specialty license plates constitute government speech that is immune from any requirement of viewpoint neutrality?

2. Does preventing the confederate flag from appearing on license plates constitute viewpoint discrimination?
description: Texas' specialty license plates constitute government speech that does not require viewpoint neutrality under the First Amendment.

name: Armstrong v. Exceptional Child Center, Inc.
question: Does the Supremacy Clause give Medicaid providers a private right of action against a state when Congress chose not to create enforceable rights under the Medicaid Act?
description: A case that determines whether or not a private right of action exists under the Medicaid Act.

name: Bank of America v. Caulkett
question: Does Section 506(d) of the Bankruptcy Code allow a debtor filing for bankruptcy to void a second mortgage when the debt owed on the first one exceeds the value of the collateral property?
description: A case in which the court ruled that Section 506 (d) of the Bankruptcy Code does not allow a debtor filing for bankruptcy to void a second mortgage when the debt owed on the first one exceeds the value of the collateral property.

name: Reyes Mata v. Lynch
question: Did the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit err in holding that it did not have the jurisdiction to review a Board of Immigration Appeals decision not to suspend the 90-day filing limitation?
description: A case in which the Court held that circuit courts of appeals have jurisdiction over Board of Immigration Appeals decisions to deny motions to reopen immigration proceedings.

name: Carroll v. Carman
question: Should Officer Carroll be entitled to qualified immunity?
description: A case in which the Court ruled that a government official is entitled to qualified immunity unless his actions violate a statute or constitutional right that was clearly established at the time of the conduct.

name: Horne v. Department of Agriculture
question:
(1) Does the Takings Clause of the Fifth Amendment apply only to real property?

(2) Can the government avoid the duty to pay just compensation for the physical taking of property by reserving the property owner a contingent interest in the value of the property?

(3) Does a per se taking occur when the government mandates the relinquishment of specific, identifiable property as a condition of permission to engage in commerce?
description: A case in which the Court determined that the reserve requirement of the Department of Agriculture’s Marketing Order constituted a per se taking and therefore required that the government provide just compensation.

name: McFadden v. United States
question: To convict someone under the Controlled Substances Analogue Act, does the government need to prove that the defendant knew the substance was an analogue to a controlled substance?
description: A case in which the Court decided that in order to fulfill the intent element of The Controlled Substance Analogue Enforcement Act of 1986, a person must either know that the substance is a controlled substance or be aware of what the substance is without knowing that it is controlled.

name: Harris v. Viegelahn
question: When a debtor in good faith converts a bankruptcy case from Chapter 13 of the Bankruptcy Code to Chapter 7, are the undistributed funds held by the Chapter 13 trustee refunded to the debtor or distributed to the creditors?
description: A case in which the Court held that any assets acquired after the date of filing for Chapter 13 bankruptcy must be returned to the debtor when the bankruptcy is converted to Chapter 7.

name: Michigan v. Environmental Protection Agency
question: Did the Environmental Protection Agency unreasonably refuse to consider costs in determining whether it was appropriate to regulate electric utility steam generating units?
description: A case in which the Court determined that the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) unreasonably interpreted the Clean Air Act by not considering costs to power plants in deciding that regulation was “appropriate and necessary.”

name: Obergefell v. Hodges
question:
(1) Does the Fourteenth Amendment require a state to license a marriage between two people of the same sex?

(2) Does the Fourteenth Amendment require a state to recognize a marriage between two people of the same sex that was legally licensed and performed in another state?
description: A case in which the Court held that the Fourteenth Amendment requires states to license and recognize same-sex marriage.

name: Kingsley v. Hendrickson
question: When the plaintiff is a pretrial detainee, are the requirements of an excessive force claim satisfied by showing that the state actor deliberately used force and the use of force was objectively unreasonable?
description: A case in which the Court held that a pretrial detainee who brings an excessive force claim need only prove that the use of force in question was objectively unreasonable.

name: Toca v. Louisiana
question:
1. Does the rule in Miller apply retroactively to juveniles sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole?

2. Does the Supreme Court have jurisdiction where a state court has failed to find a Teague exception?
description: A case in which the Court was to consider whether the rule in Miller applies retroactively to juveniles sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole, but was dismissed prior to arguments.

name: Christeson v. Roper
question:
(1) Does an actual conflict of interest meet the "interests of justice" standard and require the appointment of conflict-free counsel?

(2) Should the appointed counsel that procedurally defaulted the client's federal habeas application through an untimely filing of the petition continue their court appointment and determine the existence of pleas regarding their own abandonment and/or misconduct?
description: A case in which the Court held that an attorney’s conflict of interest with that of their client met the “interests of justice” standard and required the appointment of conflict-free counsel.

name: Glossip v. Gross
question: Does Oklahoma's use of midazolam as the initial drug in the execution protocol, the same initial drug used in Clayton Lockett's execution, violate the Eighth Amendment's prohibition against cruel and unusual punishment?
description: A case in which the Court held that the use of midazolam as the initial drug in a state’s execution protocol does not violate the Eighth Amendment’s prohibition against cruel and unusual punishment.

name: Equal Employment Opportunity Commission v. Abercrombie & Fitch Stores, Inc.
question: Can an employer be held liable under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 for refusing to hire an applicant based on a religious observance or practice if the employer did not have direct knowledge that a religious accommodation was required?
description: A case in which the Court held that an employer may be held liable under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act if an applicant can show that her need for an accommodation was a motivating factor in the employer’s decision not to hire her.

name: Glebe v. Frost
question: Was the Washington Supreme Court's decision to classify the restriction of closing arguments as trial error rather than structural error correct?
description: A case in which the Court affirmed the Washington Supreme Court’s decision to classify the restriction of closing arguments as trial error rather than structural error.

name: Woods v. Donald
question: Did the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit properly affirm the granting of federal habeas relief by holding that the Michigan Court of Appeals improperly applied Supreme Court precedent?
description: A case in which the Court held that  federal habeas relief may only be granted when a state court’s decision runs counter to clearly established federal law, and there is no precedent clearly establishing that the absence of counsel during testimony about codefendants violates a defendant’s Sixth Amendment right to effective assistance of counsel.

name: Grady v. North Carolina
question: Does wearing a GPS monitor constitute a search under the Fourth Amendment?
description: A case in which the Court held that wearing a GPS monitoring bracelet amounts to a search under the Fourth Amendment.

name: Taylor v. Barkes
question: Is there a clearly established constitutional right under the Eighth Amendment for an incarcerated person to have access to the proper implementation of adequate suicide prevention protocols?
description: A case in which the Court held that there was no clearly established constitutional right for an incarcerated person to have access to adequate suicide prevention protocols.

name: First Federal Savings & Loan Association of Boston v. Tax Commission of Massachusetts
United States v. New York Telephone Company
Cleland v. National College of Business
Crist, et al. v. Cline & Brest
J. W. Bateson Company, Inc. v. United States ex rel. Board of Trustees of National Automatic Sprinkler Industry Pension Fund
Stump v. Sparkman
question: Does a district court judge have the power to entertain and act upon the petition for sterilization, which makes him immune from damages liability even if his approval of the petition was in error?
description: A case in which the Court held that a district court judge has the power to entertain and act upon the petition for sterilization, which makes him immune from damages liability even if his approval of the petition was in error.

name: First National Bank of Boston v. Bellotti
question: Does the First Amendment protect the rights of corporations to attempt to influence the outcome of elections in which they have no direct monetary interest?

name: Owen Equipment & Erection Company v. Kroger
In re Primus
question: Can a state punish an attorney who advises someone of her legal rights and discloses that free legal assistance is available from a non-profit organization with which the attorney is affiliated?
description: A case in which the Court held that a state cannot punish an attorney who advises someone of her legal rights and discloses that free legal assistance is available from a non-profit organization with which the attorney is affiliated.

name: Mincey v. Arizona
question:
1. Did the admission of evidence taken during a four-day long warrantless search of Mincey’s residence constitute an unreasonable search or seizure under the Fourth and Fourteenth Amendments?

2. Did the admission of Mincey’s responses to police questioning made while he was a patient in the intensive care unit of a hospital violate his privilege against self-incrimination, rights to counsel and due process under the Fifth, Sixth, and Fourteenth Amendments?

name: Andrus v. Charlestone Stone Products Company
Zenith Radio Corporation v. United States
Zablocki v. Redhail
question: Did the Wisconsin statute violate the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment?

name: Christiansburg Garment Company v. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission
Hicklin v. Orbeck
question: Did the Alaska statute violate the Constitution's Privileges and Immunities Clause of Article IV, Section 2, and the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment?

name: Bordenkircher v. Hayes
question: Does the Fourteenth Amendment's Due Process Clause prohibit state prosecutors from carrying out a threat made during plea negotiations to re-indict the accused on more serious charges if he does not plead guilty to the offense with which he was originally charged?

name: Monell v. Department of Social Services of the City of New York
question: If sued in their official capacity, are local government officials and organizations such as a school board considered “persons” for the purpose of liability for back wages?

name: Pennsylvania v. Mimms
question: Do police officers violate the Fourth Amendment's prohibition against unlawful searches and seizures when, during a routine traffic stop, they obtain evidence through a search conducted after asking the suspect to exit the vehicle without a justifiable reason to do so?

name: Carey v. Piphus
question: In cases dealing with the denial of due process, must a plaintiff prove that he was actually injured by the deprivation in order to recover substantial nonpunitive damages?

name: Landmark Communications, Inc. v. Virginia
question: Did the criminal punishment of Landmark for disclosing information from the Judicial Inquiry and Review Commission's hearing violate the First Amendment?

name: National Society of Professional Engineers v. United States
United States v. United States Gypsum Company
Citizens & Southern Nat. Bank v. Bougas
American Broadcasting Companies, Inc. v. Writers Guild of America, West, Inc.
question: Does a labor union violate the National Labor Relations Act when it disciplines its members for crossing the picket line to perform collective-bargaining and grievance-adjustment tasks during a strike?
description: A case in which the Court held that a labor union violated the National Labor Relations Act when it disciplined its members for crossing the picket line to perform collective-bargaining and grievance-adjustment tasks during a strike.

name: United States v. LaSalle National Bank
Southern Overlying Carrier Chapter of the California Dump Truck Owners Association v. Public Utilities Commission of California
Michigan v. Tyler
question: Does the Fourth Amendment protection against illegal searches and seizures extend to investigations of burned premises for evidence of arson?

name: Butz v. Economou
question: Are federal administrators entitled to absolute or qualified immunity in the face of challenges to their conduct of public business?

name: National Labor Relations Board v. Local Union No. 103, International Association of Bridge, Structural & Ornamental Iron Workers, AFL-CIO
Exxon Corporation v. Governor of Maryland
question:
(1) Does Maryland's statute violate the Due Process and Commerce Clauses of the Constitution?

(2) Does Maryland's statute conflict with the Robinson-Patman Act?

name: Vermont Yankee Nuclear Power Corporation v. Natural Resources Defense Council, Inc.
Foley v. Connelie
question: Did the New York law violate the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment?

name: National Broiler Marketing Assn. v. United States
Ballew v. Georgia
question: Does a state criminal trial by a jury of only five persons deprive the accused of the right to a trial by jury as protected by the Sixth and Fourteenth Amendments?

name: United Air Lines, Inc. v. McMann
Tennessee Valley Authority v. Hill
question:
(1) Does the ESA prohibit completion of the Tellico Dam?

(2) Is the Snail Darter protected by the Endangered Species Act, even though congress continued to fund the dam project and stated that it should be completed?

name: Eastex, Inc. v. National Labor Relations Board
Massachusetts v. United States
question: Did the tax on civil aircraft violate the implied immunity of state governments from federal taxation?

name: Board of Curators of the University of Missouri v. Horowitz
question: Does an academic dismissal from a university without a hearing before the school’s decision-making body violate the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment?
description: A case in which the Court held that an academic dismissal from a university without a hearing before the school’s decision-making body did not violate the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.

name: Pfizer Inc. v. Government of India
Lockett v. Ohio
question: Did the Ohio law violate the Eighth and Fourteenth Amendments by limiting the consideration of mitigating factors?

name: Penn Central Transportation Company v. New York City
question: Did the restriction against Penn Central constitute a "taking" in violation of the Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments?

name: Beth Israel Hospital v. National Labor Relations Board
question: Was the U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit correct in upholding the part of the National Labor Relations Board's order that barred the hospital from enforcing its rule that prohibited employees from distributing union literature and soliciting support in eating facilities?

name: Hutto v. Finney
question: Did punitive isolation for more than thirty days in the Arkansas prison system constitute cruel and unusual punishment as prohibited by the Eighth and Fourteenth Amendments?

name: Federal Communications Commission v. National Citizens Committee for Broadcasting
Browder v. Director, Dept. of Corrections of Ill.
Baldwin v. Fish and Game Commission of Montana
question: Did the Montana law violate the Privileges and Immunities Clause of the Constitution as delineated in Article IV, Section 2?

name: Parker v. Flook
question: Does the identification of a limited category of useful applications of a mathematical formula, such as its use in catalytic conversion processes, render a method based on such a formula-eligible for patent protection?
description: A case in which the Court held that, absent some other novel or inventive concept in the individual’s application for a patent, activity that results from the solution of a formula or algorithm cannot transform the formula from an unpatentable principle into a patentable process.

name: McDaniel v. Paty
question: Does the Tennessee statute barring “Minister[s] of the Gospel or priest[s] of any denomination whatever” from serving as legislators violate the free exercise of religion guaranteed through the First and Fourteenth Amendments?

name: Richmond Unified School District v. Berg
United States v. California
question: Does California have jurisdiction over the submerged lands and waters under the Submerged Lands Act of 1953?

name: Zurcher v. Stanford Daily
question: Did the search of The Daily's newsroom violate the First and Fourth Amendments?

name: Commissioner of Internal Revenue v. Kowalski
United States v. Jacobs
question: If a witness in a trial is a potential defendant, should the individual be warned of their constitutionally-protected rights against self-incrimination?
description: A case in which the Court declined to answer the question of whether, if a witness in a trial is a potential defendant, the individual should be warned of their constitutionally-protected rights against self-incrimination.

name: Adamo Wrecking Company v. United States
Duke Power Company v. Carolina Environmental Study Group, Inc.
Memphis Light, Gas & Water Division v. Craft
Sears, Roebuck & Company v. San Diego County District Council of Carpenters
Greyhound Corporation v. Mt. Hood Stages, Inc.
Federal Communications Commission v. Pacifica Foundation
question: Does the First Amendment deny government any power to restrict the public broadcast of indecent language under any circumstances?
description: A case in which the Court held that audience, medium, time of day and method of transmission were all relevant factors in determining what speech is protected by the First Amendment.

name: Department of Revenue of Washington v. Association of Washington Stevedoring Companies
Kulko v. Superior Court of Cal., City and County of San Francisco
Houchins v. KQED Inc.
question: Did the First Amendment guarantee news media a right of access to jails over and above that of other persons?

name: Will v. Calvert Fire Insurance Company
Flagg Bros., Inc. v. Brooks
question: Does a New York state statute that allows storage companies to sell stored goods if they do not receive payment violate the Fourteenth Amendment?

name: Allied Structural Steel Company v. Spannaus
question: Did Minnesota's Private Pension Benefits Protection Act violate the Contract Clause of the Constitution?

name: National Labor Relations Board v. Robbins Tire & Rubber Company
St. Paul Fire & Marine Insurance Company v. Barry
City of Philadelphia v. New Jersey
question: Did New Jersey's waste importation law violate the Commerce Clause?

name: United States Steel Corporation v. Multistate Tax Commission
question: Did the formation of this group violate the the Compact Clause of Article I?

name: Idaho Department of Employment v. Smith
Holloway v. Arkansas
question: Does requiring a single attorney to represent multiple defendants deprive the defendants of their Sixth Amendment right to adequate assistance of counsel?

name: Regents of the University of California v. Bakke
question: Did the University of California violate the Fourteenth Amendment's equal protection clause, and the Civil Rights Act of 1964, by practicing an affirmative action policy that resulted in the repeated rejection of Bakke's application for admission to its medical school?
description: A case in which the Court found that any racial quota for the purpose of admissions supported by a government entity violates the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.

name: Federal Maritime Commission v. Pacific Maritime Assn
United States v. Board of Commissioners of Sheffield, Alabama
Raymond Motor Transportation, Inc. v. Rice
Frank Lyon Company v. United States
City of Lafayette v. Louisiana Power & Light Company
Central Illinois Public Service Company v. United States
County Bd. of Arlington County, Virginia v. Richards
Chase Manhattan Bank (National Association) v. South Acres Development Company
City of Los Angeles Department of Water and Power v. Manhart
question:
Does a policy that requires women to make larger contributions to a company’s pension plan than men because women tend to live longer violate the Civil Rights Act of 1964?

Is the company liable for the amount of the excess payment?

name: Securities and Exchange Commission v. Sloan
question:
1. Is a challenge to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) over its exercise of the authority to suspend the trading of stock of a particular company moot if the SEC asserts it has no plans to consider further orders against that company?
  2. Does § 12(k) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 permit the Commission to issue consecutive orders for the suspension of trading of a particular company's stock?
description: A case in which the Court held that the Securities and Exchange Commission lacks authority under § 12(k) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 to issue multiple consecutive 10-day orders for the suspension of trading of a company's stock.

name: Ohralik v. Ohio State Bar Assn.
question: Do professional ethics rules for the legal profession that ban in-person solicitation of non-lawyers violate free speech guarantees under the First and Fourteenth Amendments?
description: A case in which the Court held that a state may constitutionally discipline a lawyer for soliciting clients in person and for financial gain under circumstances likely to pose dangers that the state has a right to prevent.

name: Agosto v. Immigration and Naturalization Service
United States v. Raddatz
question: Does the statute allowing the district court to decide a suppression motion based on a record and finding of facts developed by a magistrate judge violate the Constitution?

name: GTE Sylvania, Inc. v. Consumers Union of the United States, Inc.
Norfolk & Western Railway Company v. Liepelt
Consumer Product Safety Commission v. GTE Sylvania, Inc.
Central Machinery Company v. Arizona State Tax Commission
Board of Education of the City of School District of New York
Curtiss-Wright Corporation v. General Elec. Company
National Labor Relations Board v. Yeshiva University
Kissinger v. Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press
Harris v. McRae
question: Did the Hyde Amendment violate the right to privacy, the Due Process Clause of the Fifth Amendment, or the Religion Clauses of the First Amendment?

name: Chiarella v. United States
question: Did Chiarella violate Section 10(b) of the 1934 Act by failing to disclose the impending takeover before trading in the target company's securities?

name: City of Rome v. United States
General Telephone Company of the Northwest, Inc. v. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission
Crowell v. Mader Judgment vacated and case remanded
Richmond Newspapers Inc. v. Virginia
question: Did the closure of the trial to the press and public violate the First Amendment or the Sixth Amendment?

name: Vance v. Universal Amusement Company, Inc.
Crown Simpson Pulp Company v. Costle
question: Did the court of appeals have jurisdiction over the permit review where the State of California was in charge of granting the permit?

name: Rush v. Savchuk
question: Can a state have jurisdiction over a defendant with no connections in the state by attaching the contractual obligation of an insurer licensed in the state?
description: A case in which the Court held that a state could not acquire jurisdiction over a defendant with no connections in the state by attaching the contractual obligation of an insurer licensed in the state?

name: Diamond v. Chakrabarty
question: Is the creation of a live, human-made organism patentable under Title 35 U.S.C. Section 101?

name: Strycker's Bay Neighborhood Council, Inc. v. Karlen
Dawson Chemical Company v. Rohm & Haas Company
National Labor Relations Board v. Retail Store Employees Union
McLain v. Real Estate Board of New Orleans, Inc.
United States v. Sioux Nation of Indians
question:
(1) Was Congress' 1978 amendment a violation of separation of powers?

(2) Was the reclamation of land in 1877 a taking of property requiring compensation under the Just Compensation Clause of the Fifth Amendment?

name: Mobil Oil Corporation v. Commissioner of Taxes of Vermont
World-Wide Volkwagen Corporation v. Woodson
question: May a state court exercise in personam jurisdiction over a non-resident defendant in a products liability action where the defendant’s only connection to the state is the accident in question?

name: Lewis v. BT Investment Managers, Inc.
Secretary of the Navy v. Huff
Village of Schaumburg v. Citizens for Better Environment
question: Was Schaumburg's ordinance "overbroad" and therefore in violation of the First and Fourteenth Amendments?

name: Estes v. Metropolitan Branches of Dallas National Association for the Advancement of Colored People
Rhode Island v. Innis
question: Did the police "interrogation" en route to the station violate Innis's Miranda rights?

name: Exxon Corporation v. Department of Rev. of Wisconsin
United States Parole Commission v. Geraghty
California Retail Liquor Dealers Assn. v. Midcal Aluminum, Inc.
Walter v. United States
question: Is the warrantless projection of films a violation of the Fourth Amendment?

name: Williams v. Zbaraz
question:
(1) Did the district court have the jurisdiction to consider the constitutionality of the Hyde Amendment?

(2) Does the Hyde Amendment allow a state to limit its Medicaid funding of abortions to those specified by the Amendment?

name: Martinez v. California
question: Does a statute immunizing parole officials from injuries resulting from parole decisions violate the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment?
description: A case in which the Court held that a statute immunizing parole officials from injuries resulting from parole decisions violate the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.

name: Snepp v. United States
question: Were Snepp's First Amendment rights violated?

name: Catalano, Inc. v. Target Sales, Inc.
Seatrain Shipbuilding Corporation v. Shell Oil Company
Sears, Roebuck and Co. v. County of Los Angeles and City of Compton
question: Is the County of Los Angeles tax an unconstitutional regulation on interstate commerce?

name: Central Hudson Gas & Electric Corporation v. Public Service Commission of New York
question: Did the PSC's ban on advertising violate the freedom of speech protected by the First and Fourteenth Amendments?

name: United States v. California
question: Do man-made piers and islands qualify as "coast line" under the Submerged Lands Act of 1953?

name: Deposit Guaranty National Bank of Jackson v. Roper
Consolidated Edison Company of New York v. Public Service Commission of New York
United States v. Benmar Transp. & Leasing Corporation
Nachman Corporation v. Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation
Board of Regents of Univ. of State of N. Y. v. Tomanio
Reeves Inc. v. Stake
question: Did South Dakota's preferential system violate the Commerce Clause?

name: Fullilove v. Klutznick
question: Did the provision of the statute for minority business enterprises violate the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment?

name: Washington v. Confederated Tribes of the Colville Indian Reservation
O'Bannon v. Town Court Nursing Center
Aaron v. SEC
question: Must the SEC prove that that the defendant intended to “deceive, manipulate, or defraud” in an action that alleges violations of Section 17(a) of the ’33 Act and Section 10(b) of the ’34 Act and Rule 10b-5?
description: A case in which the Court held that plain language and the legislative history of the statutes required the SEC to establish defendant’s intent to “deceive, manipulate, or defraud” for violations of Section 10(b) and the part of Section 17(a) that specifically refers to the use of a device, scheme, or artifice with intent to defraud.

name: National Labor Relations Board v. International Longshoremen's Association, AFL-CIO
Bloomer v. Liberty Mutual Insurance Company
Ohio v. Roberts
question: Does the introduction into evidence of prior testimony of a witness who had not been cross-examined violate the Sixth Amendment?

name: Idaho ex rel. Evans v. Oregon
American Export Lines, Inc. v. Alvez
question: May Alvez’s wife sue American Export Lines, Inc. for loss of consortium, as a result of AELI’s negligence and the unseaworthiness of the USS Export Builder, under federal maritime law?

name: Goldwater v. Carter
question: Did Congress have a constitutional role to play in the termination of the treaty?

name: PruneYard Shopping Center v. Robins
question: Did PruneYard's regulations violate the students' free speech rights?

name: Supreme Court of Virginia v. Consumers Union of the United States, Inc.
question:
Is the Supreme Court of Virginia immune from a suit brought under the Civil Rights Code of 1983?

Can the Supreme Court of Virginia be liable for attorney’s fees?

name: White Mountain Apache Tribe v. Bracker
Ybarra v. Illinois
question: Does the Illinois state statute that allows authorities to search persons on the premises during the execution of a valid search warrant violate the Fourth and Fourteenth Amendments?

name: Committee for Public Education and Religious Liberty v. Regan
New York Gaslight Club, Inc. v. Carey
Rummel v. Estelle
question: Did Rummel's life sentence under the Texas recidivist law constitute cruel and unusual punishment in violation of the Eighth Amendment?

name: Ford Motor Credit Company v. Milhollin
Wengler v. Druggists Mutual Insurance Company
Godfrey v. Georgia
question: Is the Georgia law governing the death penalty “arbitrary and capricious” in violation of the Eighth Amendment?

name: Industrial Union Department, AFL-CIO v. American Petroleum Institute
question: Did the Secretary exceed his authority to set standards?

name: Hatzlachh Supply Company, Inc. v. United States
Thomas v. Washington Gas Light Company
Trammel v. United States
question: Is it a reversible error to permit a wife to be called as a witness against her husband over his objection and without his consent?
description: A case in which the Court held that it is not eversible error to permit a wife to be called as a witness against her husband over his objection and without his consent.

name: Carbon Fuel Company v. United Mine Workers of America
Chickasaw Nation v. United States
question: Does the Indian Regulatory Gaming Act exempt tribes from paying the gambling-related taxes, which State need not pay, imposed by chapter 35 of the Internal Revenue Code?

name: Sao Paulo State of Federative Republic of Brazil v. American Tobacco Company, Inc.
question: Should a judge be removed from a case when his name previously appeared on a brief for a case involving one of the parties?
description: A case in which the Court held that the standard for removing a judge from a case based on potential partiality is whether a reasonable person, knowing all the circumstances, would expect the judge in question to have actual knowledge of his bias or partiality.

name: Swierkiewicz v. Sorema N.A.
question: Must a complaint in an employment discrimination lawsuit contain specific facts establishing a prima facie case of discrimination?

name: Toyota Manufacturing, Kentucky, Inc. v. Williams
question: Did the Court of Appeals use the proper standard in determining whether an employee was disabled under the ADA due to carpal tunnel syndrome by showing that her manual disability involved a class of manual activities affecting the ability to perform tasks at work?

name: US Airways, Inc. v. Barnett
question: Does the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 require an employer to reassign a disabled employee to a position as a reasonable accommodation even though another employee is entitled to hold the position under the employer's seniority system?

name: Chao v. Mallard Bay Drilling, Inc.
question: Does the Occupational Safety and Health Administration have jurisdiction under the Occupational Safety and Health Act to issue citations to uninspected vessels, which are subject to minimal Coast Guard regulation?

name: Thompson v. Western States Medical Center
question: Do the prohibitions in the Food and Drug Administration Modernization Act of 1997 with regard to soliciting prescriptions for, and advertising, compounded drugs violate the First Amendment?

name: Dusenbery v. United States
question: Does the FBI's notice of intended forfeiture by sending certified letters to inmates while incarcerated satisfy due process?

name: Adams v. Florida Power Corp.
question: May disparate impact claims be brought under the Age Discrimination in Employment Act of 1967?

name: Zelman v. Simmons-Harris
question: Does Ohio's school voucher program violate the Establishment Clause?
description: A case in which the Court held that Ohio’s Pilot Project Scholarship Program did not violate the Establishment Clause while providing school tuition vouchers eligible for use at religiously-affiliated schools.

name: Chevron U.S.A., Inc. v. Echazabal
question: Does the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 permit the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission's regulation that allows the defense that a worker's disability on the job would pose a direct threat to his health?

name: Mathias v. WorldCom Technologies, Inc.
question: Is a state commission's action relating to the enforcement of an interconnection agreement under the Telecommunications Act of 1996 reviewable in federal court? Does a state commission waive its Eleventh Amendment immunity by voluntarily participating in the regulatory scheme established by the Act? Does the doctrine of Ex parte Young permit suit for relief against state public utility commissioners in their official capacities for alleged ongoing violations of the Act?

name: Department of Housing and Urban Development v. Rucker
question: Does the Anti-Drug Abuse Act of 1988, as amended, allow local public housing agencies to evict tenants for drug-related activity of non-tenant relatives or guests regardless of whether tenants knew, or should have known, about the activity?

name: BE & K Construction Company v. National Labor Relations Board
question: Did the Court of Appeals err in holding that the National Labor Relations Board may impose liability on an employer for filing a losing retaliatory lawsuit, even if the employer could show the suit was not objectively baseless?

name: Securities and Exchange Commission v. Zandford
question: Is the alleged fraudulent conduct of a securities broker, who sells his customer's securities and using the proceeds for his own benefit without the customer's knowledge or consent, in connection with the purchase or sale of any security within the meaning of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and SEC Rule 10b-5?

name: Christopher v. Harbury
question: Does the charge that an official deception denied a plaintiff access to the courts by leaving her without information or reason to seek information, with which she could have brought a lawsuit, state an actionable claim?

name: Gisbrecht v. Barnhart
question: Do lodestar fee awards for attorneys who successfully represent Social Security benefits claimants in court, under 42 USC section 406(b), displace contingent-fee agreements within the statutory ceiling?

name: Board of Ed. of Independent School Dist. No. 92 of Pottawatomie Cty. v. Earls
question: Is the Student Activities Drug Testing Policy, which requires all students who participate in competitive extracurricular activities to submit to drug testing, consistent with the Fourth Amendment?
description: A case in which the Court held that an Oklahoma public school's random drug testing of its students was constitutional, since the policy reasonably served the district's important interest in detecting and preventing drug use in its student body.

name: Wisconsin Department of Health and Family Services v. Blumer
question: Is the income-first method of determining whether a community spouse is entitled to a higher community spouse resource allowance consistent with the Medicare Catastrophic Coverage Act of 1988?

name: Kelly v. South Carolina
question: Did the state trial court err in holding Simmons v. South Carolina, 512 U.S. 154 inapposite in the death sentence proceeding of William Kelly?

name: Harris v. United States
question: Is McMillan v. Pennsylvania, 477 U.S. 79, valid after the U.S. Supreme Court's decision in Apprendi v. New Jersey, 530 U.S. 466?

name: Alabama v. Shelton
question: Does the Sixth Amendment right to appointed counsel, as defined in Argersinger v. Hamlin, 407 U.S. 25, and Scott v. Illinois, 440 U.S. 367, apply to a defendant who was sentenced to a suspended sentence?

name: McKune v. Lile
question: Does the Kansas Sexual Abuse Treatment Program violate inmates' Fifth Amendment privilege against compelled self-incrimination?

name: Federal Maritime Commission v. South Carolina State Ports Authority
question: Does a State's sovereign immunity preclude the Federal Maritime Commission from adjudicating a private party's complaint that a state-run port has violated the Shipping Act of 1984?

name: Mickens v. Taylor
question: Must a defendant show that a conflict of interest adversely affected his representation in order to demonstrate a Sixth Amendment violation when the trial court fails to inquire into a potential conflict of interest about which it knew or reasonably should have known?

name: United States v. Cotton
question: Does the omission from a federal indictment of a fact that enhances the statutory maximum sentence justify a Court of Appeals' vacating the enhanced sentence, even though the defendant did not object in the trial court?

name: Rush Prudential HMO, Inc. v. Moran
question: Is the Illinois Health Maintenance Organization Act, as applied to health benefits provided by a health maintenance organization under contract with an employee welfare benefit plan, preempted by the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974?

name: Thomas v. Chicago Park District
question: Must a municipal park ordinance requiring individuals to obtain a permit before conducting large-scale events must, consistent with the First Amendment, contain certain procedural safeguards?

name: Stewart v. Smith

timeline.event: Certified question to Arizona Supreme Court

question: Did the Court of Appeals err in interpreting Arizona law concerning its postconviction-relief rule?
description: In determining whether procedural default barred federal habeas corpus review of Arizona prisoner's ineffective-assistance-of-counsel claim, Arizona waiver determination is independent of federal law.

name: United States v. Bass
question: Must a defendant seeking discovery against the United States government on a claim of selective prosecution show evidence that similarly-situated defendants of a different race were not prosecuted?
description: A case in which the Court held that a defendant who is seeking discovery against the United States government for a claim of selective prosecution must produce evidence of discriminatory effect and intent.

name: Adarand Constructors, Inc. v. Mineta
question: Did the Court of Appeals misapply the strict scrutiny standard in determining if Congress had a compelling interest to enact legislation designed to remedy the effects of racial discrimination? Is the U.S. Department of Transportation's current Disadvantaged Business Enterprise program narrowly tailored to serve a compelling governmental interest?

name: Equal Employment Opportunity Commission v. Waffle House, Inc.
question: Does an agreement between an employer and an employee to arbitrate employment-related disputes bar the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission from pursuing victim-specific judicial relief in an enforcement action alleging that the employer has violated Title I of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990?

name: Horn v. Banks
question: Did the Court of Appeals err by failing to perform an analysis of whether Mills v. Maryland, 486 U.S. 367, applied retroactively to cases on federal habeas corpus review under Teague v. Lane, 489 U.S. 288?

name: Great-West Life and Annuity Insurance Company v. Knudson
question: Does the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 authorize a suit to enforce a reimbursement provision by a health plan to recover from a beneficiary any proceeds paid by a third party?

name: Carey v. Saffold
question: Does the word "pending," in the Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act of 1996, cover the time between a lower state court's decision and the filing of a notice of appeal to a higher state court? If so, does it apply similarly to California's unique state collateral review system?

name: Porter v. Nussle
question: Does the Prison Litigation Reform Act of 1995 require that all prisoners seeking redress for prison circumstances or occurrences exhaust any applicable administrative remedies before filing suit?

name: TRW Inc. v. Andrews
question: Does the Fair Credit Reporting Act's two-year statute of limitations governing actions to enforce any liability created by the act commence to run only upon a party's discovery of alleged violations of the act?

name: Barnhart v. Walton
question: Does the term "inability," in the Social Security Act, include a 12 month requirement, such that the inability must last, or must be expected to last, for at least 12 months? Is the term "expected to last" applicable only when the "inability" has not yet lasted 12 months?

name: Ring v. Arizona
question: Does Arizona's capital sentencing scheme violate the Sixth Amendment's jury trial guarantee by entrusting to a judge the finding of facts sufficient to impose the death penalty?

name: Hoffman Plastic Compounds, Inc. v. National Labor Relations Board
question: Does the National Labor Relations Board have the discretion to award backpay to an undocumented alien employee who was not legally authorized to work in the United States?

name: Barnhart v. Sigmon Coal Company, Inc.
question: Does the Coal Industry Retiree Health Benefit Act of 1992 permit the Commissioner of Social Security to assign retired miners to the successors in interest of out-of-business signatory operators?

name: Holmes Group, Inc. v. Vornado Air Circulation Systems, Inc.
question: Does the Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit have appellate jurisdiction over a case in which the complaint does not allege a claim arising under federal patent law, but the answer contains a patent-law counterclaim?

name: Kansas v. Crane
question: Did the Kansas Supreme Court interpret Kansas v. Hendricks in an overly restrictive manner by ruling that it requires a finding that a sexual offender, who has only an emotional or personality disorder, rather than a volitional impairment, has an inability to control dangerous behavior?

name: Festo Corporation v. Shoketsu Kinzoku Kogyo Kabushiki Company
question: Does a patentee, by narrowing a claim to obtain a patent, surrender all equivalents to the amended claim element?

name: United States v. Fior D'Italia, Inc.
question: Does the law, under which the Federal Insurance Contribution Act taxes are paid, authorize the IRS to assess a restaurant for FICA taxes based upon its aggregate estimate of all the tips that the restaurant's customers paid its employees?

name: JPMorgan Chase Bank v. Traffic Stream (BVI) Infrastructure Ltd.
question: Is a corporation organized under the laws of the British Virgin Islands a "citizen or subject of a foreign state" for the purposes of alienage diversity jurisdiction?

name: United States v. Arvizu
question: Did a border agent have reasonable suspicion to believe that Ralph Arvizu was engaged in illegal activity based on a number of factors?

name: Tahoe-Sierra Preservation Council, Inc. v. Tahoe Regional Planning Agency
question: Does a moratorium on development imposed during the process of devising a comprehensive land-use plan constitutes a per se taking of property requiring compensation under the Fifth Amendment's Takings Clause?

name: Ashcroft v. American Civil Liberties Union
question: Does the Child Online Protection Act's use of "community standards" to identify "material that is harmful to minors" violate the First Amendment?

name: National Railroad Passenger Corporation v. Morgan
question: May a plaintiff, under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, sue on employment discrimination claims that fall outside the statute's 300-day limit? May a plaintiff sue on claims that fall outside the period so long as the claims contribute to claims that took place within the period?

name: Atkins v. Virginia
question: Is the execution of mentally retarded persons "cruel and unusual punishment" prohibited by the Eighth Amendment?
description: A case in which the Court found that sentencing a mentally disabled person to death is a violation of the Eighth Amendment's Cruel and Unusual Punishment Clause.

name: Correctional Services Corporation v. Malesko
question: Should the implied private action for damages against federal officers alleged to have violated a citizen's constitutional rights, first recognized in Bivens v. Six Unknown Fed. Narcotics Agents, 403 U.S. 388, be extended to allow recovery against a private corporation operating a halfway house under contract with the Bureau of Prisons?

name: Owasso Independent School District No. I-011 v. Falvo
question: Does the practice of peer grading violate the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act of 1974?

name: United States v. Knights
question: Does a search pursuant to a common California probation condition, supported by reasonable suspicion, satisfy the Fourth Amendment?

name: Ragsdale v. Wolverine World Wide, Inc.
question: Does Labor Department regulation 29 CFR section 825.700(a) require employers to grant an employee additional leave after granting more than 12 weeks of leave, if the employer failed to notify the employee that the original leave counted against the employee's Family and Medical Leave Act of 1993 entitlement?

name: New York v. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
question: May the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission require a public utility to transmit competitors' electricity over its lines on the same terms that the utility applies to its own energy transmissions, if the utility unbundles, or separates, the cost of transmission from the cost of electrical energy when billing its retail customers? Must FERC impose that requirement on utilities that continue to offer only bundled retail sales?

name: Ashcroft v. Free Speech Coalition
question: Does the Child Pornography Prevention Act of 1996 abridge freedom of speech when it proscribes a significant universe of speech that is neither obscene under Miller v. California nor child pornography under New York v. Ferber?

name: National Cable and Telecommunications Association v. Gulf Power Company
question: Does the Pole Attachments Act cover attachments that provide both cable television and high-speed Internet service? Does the Act cover attachments by wireless telecommunications providers?

name: United States v. Drayton
question: Must police officers, while searching buses at random to ask questions and to request passengers' consent to searches, advise passengers of their right not to cooperate?

name: Verizon Communications, Inc. v. Federal Communications Commission
question: Does the Telecommunications Act of 1996 authorize the Federal Communications Commission to require state utility commissions to set the rates charged by the incumbents for leased elements on a forward-looking basis untied to the incumbents' investment? Does the Act require incumbents to combine such elements at the entrants' request when they lease them to the entrants?

name: City of Los Angeles v. Alameda Books, Inc.
question: May a city rely on a study it conducted to demonstrate whether an ordinance serves a substantial government interest?

name: City of Columbus v. Ours Garage and Wrecker Service, Inc.
question: May the state power reserved in 49 USC section 14501(c)(2)(A) be delegated to municipalities, permitting them to exercise safety regulatory authority over local tow-truck operations?

name: J. E. M. Ag Supply, Inc. v. Pioneer Hi-Bred International, Inc.
question: May utility patents be issued for plants under 35 USC section 101?

name: Watchtower Bible & Tract Soc'y of New York, Inc. v. Village of Stratton
question: Does a municipal ordinance that requires a permit prior to engaging in the door-to-door advocacy of a political cause and to display upon demand the permit, which contains one's name, violate the First Amendment protection accorded to anonymous pamphleteering or discourse?

name: Utah v. Evans
question: Does the Census Bureau's use of "hot-deck imputation," in the 2000 census, violate the statutory provision forbidding use of the statistical method known as sampling? Is this methodology inconsistent with the Constitution's statement that an "actual Enumeration be made?

name: Lapides v. Board of Regents of University System of Georgia
question: Does a State's act of removing a lawsuit from state court to federal court waive the State's Eleventh Amendment immunity from suit in federal court by citizens of other States?

name: Gonzaga University v. Doe
question: May a student sue a private university for damages to enforce provisions of the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act of 1974?

name: United States v. Craft
question: Does a tenant by the entirety possess property or rights to property to which a federal lien may attach?

name: United States v. Ruiz
question: Do the Fifth and Sixth Amendments require federal prosecutors, before entering into a binding plea agreement with a criminal defendant, to disclose impeachment information relating to any informants or other witnesses?

name: Verizon Maryland, Inc. v. Public Service Commission of Maryland
question: Do federal district courts have jurisdiction over a telecommunication carrier's claim that the order of a state utility commission requiring reciprocal compensation for telephone calls to Internet Service Providers violates the Telecommunications Act of 1996?

name: Young v. United States
question: Is the Bankruptcy Code's "three-year lookback period," under which a discharge does not extinguish certain tax liabilities for which a return was due within three years before the filing of an individual debtor's petition, tolled during the pendency of a prior bankruptcy petition?

name: Barnes v. Gorman
question: May punitive damages be awarded in a private cause of action brought under the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 and the Rehabilitation Act of 1973?

name: Devlin v. Scardelletti
question: Does a nonnamed member of a class certified under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23(b)(1) have the power to appeal the approval of a settlement over objections he stated at the fairness hearing?

name: United States v. Vonn
question: Does a criminal defendant who lets a Federal Rule of Criminal Procedure Rule 11 error pass without objection in the trial court bear the burden of showing plain error under Rule 52? May a court reviewing Rule 11 error examine the entire record begun at the defendant's first appearance in the matter leading to his eventual plea when considering the effect of any error on the defendant's substantial rights?

name: United States Postal Service v. Gregory
question: Must the Merit Systems Protection Board adopt the Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit ruling that, when assessing a penalty's reasonableness, the Board may not consider prior disciplinary actions that are pending in collectively bargained grievance proceedings?

name: Bell v. Cone
question: Does defense counsel render ineffective assistance during the sentencing phase of a murder trial by failing to present mitigating evidence and waiving final argument?

name: Edelman v. Lynchburg College
question: Is the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission's regulation, which permits the verification of a timely filed discrimination charge after the limitations period, valid?

name: Raygor v. Regents of University of Minnesota
question: Does the federal supplemental jurisdiction statute's tolling provision apply to claims filed in federal court against nonconsenting States?

name: Lee v. Kemna
question: Is a defendant's imperfect compliance with Missouri court rules an adequate state ground to preclude the federal habeas corpus review of his claim that a Missouri trial judge's refusal to grant an overnight continuance violated due process?

name: Republican Party of Minnesota v. White
question: Does the First Amendment permit the Minnesota Supreme Court to prohibit candidates for judicial election in that State from announcing their views on disputed legal and political issues?

name: Franconia Associates v. United States
question: Does the Emergency Low Income Housing Preservation Act of 1987, which restricted the right of property owners to prepay at any time mortgages under the Housing Act of 1949, constitute a present breach of contract?

name: Hope v. Pelzer
question: Does the Court of Appeals holding of qualified immunity where prison guards' conduct violated the Eighth Amendment comport with United States v. Lanier, 520 U.S. 259?

name: FW/PBS, Inc. v. City of Dallas
Lewis v. Jeffers
question:
Can a federal district court conduct an independent review of the evidence of a state court’s finding of a constitutional aggravating circumstance?

Did Arizona’s construction of the “especially heinous…or depraved” aggravating circumstance contravene Supreme Court precedent?
description: A case in which the Court held that federal habeas corpus relief is not intended to find error in state laws but rather to determine whether a state court’s finding was so arbitrary and capricious that it violates the Eighth Amendment.

name: United States v. Eichman
question: Did the Act violate freedom of expression protected by the First Amendment?
description: A case in which the Court held that a federal law criminalizing the burning of an American flag violated the freedom of expression guaranteed by the First Amendment.

name: Baltimore City Department of Social Services v. Bouknight
Illinois v. Rodriguez
question:
(1) Is a police officer's good faith reliance on a third party's apparent authority to consent to a search a valid exception to the warrant requirement of the Fourth Amendment?

(2) Did the woman possess actual authority to permit a consensual entry?

name: Jimmy Swaggart Ministries v. Board of Equalization of California
question: Did California's imposition of a sales and use tax on the sale of religious materials violate the Free Exercise or Establishment Clauses of the First Amendment?

name: Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation v. LTV Corporation
Board of Education of Westside Community Schools v. Mergens By and Through Mergens
question: Was Westside's prohibition against the formation of a Christian club consistent with the Establishment Clause, thereby rendering the Equal Access Act unconstitutional?
description: A case in which the Court held that the Equal Access Act stopped Westside High School from prohibiting the formation of religious-based non-curricular student clubs.

name: Franchise Tax Board of California v. Alcan Aluminium, Limited
Guidry v. Sheet Metal Workers National Pension Fund
Pennsylvania v. Muniz
question: Do incriminating utterances of a drunk-driving suspect constitute self-incrimination under the Fifth Amendment?
description: A case in which the Court held that the Fifth Amendment distinguishes between real or physical evidence and testimonial evidence, of which only testimonial evidence is protected under the Amendment.

name: California v. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
Michigan Citizens for Independent Press v. Thornburgh
Illinois v. Perkins
question: Did the undercover police officer violate the accused's Miranda rights as protected by the Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments?

name: Rutan v. Republican Party of Illinois
question: Did Governor Thompson's practices in Illinois infringe upon the First Amendment rights of potential and current state employees?

name: W.S. Kirkpatrick & Company, Inc. v. Environmental Tectonics Corporation, International
question: Does state doctrine prohibit a US court from adjudicating a case that would attribute unlawful acts to foreign officials acting in their official capacity?
description: A case in which the Court held that state doctrine only applies when the case requires a US court to declare an act of a foreign sovereign nation invalid.

name: Chauffeurs, Teamsters and Helpers Local No. 391 v. Terry
Florida v. Wells
question: Does the Fourth Amendment allow the police to open closed containers during an inventory search where the suspect gave permission to open the truck where the container was found?
description: A case in which the Court held that the Fourth Amendment does not allow the police to open closed containers during an inventory search where the suspect gave permission to open the truck where the container was found.

name: Peel v. Attorney Registration and Disciplinary Commission of Illinois
question: Does listing National Board of Trial Advocacy certifications on an attorney's letterhead have the potential to mislead the public to an extent that warrants a categorical ban of that type of advertising?

name: Portland Golf Club v. Commissioner of Internal Revenue
United States Department of Labor v. Triplett
Eli Lilly and Company v. Medtronic, Inc.
question: Are activities that would normally constitute patent infringement excused if they are used to develop and submit information to the Food and Drug Administration to obtain marketing approval for a medical device?
description: A case in which the Court decided whether activities that would normally constitute patent infringement are excused if they are used to develop and submit information to the Food and Drug Administration to obtain marketing approval for a medical device.

name: Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation v. Feeney
Sisson v. Ruby
question: Does a federal district court have jurisdiction over a suit to limit the liability of a yacht owner regarding the fire on his vessel?
description: A case in which the Court held that the district court has maritime jurisdiction when the incident in question represents a potential hazard to maritime commerce and bears a substantial relationship to maritime activity.

name: Burnham v. Superior Court of California, County of Marin
question: Does the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment prohibit state courts from exercising jurisdiction over a nonresident who was temporarily in the state and was personally served with process in a suit unrelated to his presence in the state?
description: A case in which the Court held that states have jurisdiction over nonresidents within their borders.

name: Dole v. United Steelworkers of America
Austin v. Michigan Chamber of Commerce
question: Did the Michigan Campaign Finance Act violate the First and Fourteenth Amendments?

name: Pennsylvania Department of Public Welfare v. Davenport
Idaho v. Wright
question: Does the admission at trial of hearsay testimony made by a child to an examining pediatrician violate the Confrontation Clause of the Sixth Amendment?
description: A case in which the Court held that hearsay testimony made by a child to an examining pediatrician admitted at trial violates the Confrontation Clause of the Sixth Amendment.

name: Ohio v. Akron Center for Reproductive Health
question: Do the judicial bypass requirements, the physician notification element, and the burden of proof mandated by the parental notification bill violate a minor’s Fourteenth Amendment due process rights?
description: A case in which the Court held that an Ohio bill requiring physicians to notify the parents of an unmarried minor who is requesting an abortion did not violate a minor’s right to due process under the Fourteenth Amendment.

name: Adams Fruit Company, Inc. v. Barrett
Federal Trade Commission v. Superior Court Trial Lawyers Association
Employment Division, Department of Human Resources of Oregon v. Smith
question: Can a state deny unemployment benefits to a worker fired for using illegal drugs for religious purposes?
description: A case in which the Court held that the First Amendment does not protect individuals engaging in illegal acts as part of a religious ceremony.

name: United States v. Montalvo-Murillo
question: Did the district court err in holding that the defendant must be released as a remedy for the government’s failure to hold a timely detention hearing?
description: A case in which the Court held that the district court erred in holding that the defendant must be released as a remedy for the government’s failure to hold a timely detention hearing.

name: Alabama v. White
question: Does an anonymous tip alone provide a reasonable suspicion sufficient to stop and search an individual’s car?

name: Howlett By and Through Howlett v. Rose
Lujan v. National Wildlife Federation
question: Does an organization representing private citizens who use public land "in the vicinity" of areas affected by Bureau of Land Management (BLM) land-use designations have standing to challenge those designations under section 10(e) of the Administrative Procedure Act? Does standing to challenge several individual BLM decision confer standing to challenge those decisions as a whole, even when the organization's members are not affected by the bulk of the decisions?

name: Metro Broadcasting, Inc. v. Federal Communications Commission
question: Did the FCC's minority preference policies violate the equal protection component of the Fifth Amendment?

name: National Labor Relations Board v. Curtin Matheson Scientific, Inc.
Keller v. State Bar of California
Missouri v. Jenkins
question: Did the court order to increase property taxes violate Article III, the Tenth Amendment, or principles of federal/state comity?

name: Chesapeake and Ohio Railway Company v. Schwalb
Walton v. Arizona
question: Are the Arizona state statutes governing death penalty sentencing constitutional under the Sixth Amendment?
description: A case in which the Court held that the Arizona method of death penalty sentencing is not arbitrary and does not place an undue burden on the defendant.

name: Pavelic & LeFlore v. Marvel Entertainment Group, A Division of Cadence Industries Corporation
United States v. Goodyear Tire and Rubber Company
United Steelworkers of America, AFL-CIO-CLC v. Rawson
Maryland v. Craig
question: Did the closed-circuit testimony violate the Confrontation Clause of the Sixth Amendment?

name: John Doe Agency v. John Doe Corporation
Horton v. California
question: Does the Fourth Amendment prohibit the warrantless seizure of evidence in plain sight if the discovery of such evidence was not inadvertent?

name: United States v. Energy Resources Company, Inc.
Georgia v. South Carolina
question: What is the proper boundary between Georgia and South Carolina?

name: Office of Personnel Management v. Richmond
question: Does receipt of erroneous information from a government employee entitle a claimant to benefits he would not otherwise receive?

name: Yellow Freight System, Inc. v. Donnelly
United States v. Verdugo-Urquidez
question: Does the Fourth Amendment apply to the search and seizure by United States agents of property that is owned by a nonresident alien and located in a foreign country?

name: Breininger v. Sheet Metal Workers International Association Local Union No. 6
Wilder v. Virginia Hospital Association
question: Did the Boren Amendment create a "right" under the definition of 42 U.S.C. 1983, therefore allowing private parties to bring suit challenging the state's finding that its Medicaid reimbursement rates are "reasonable and adequate"? If such a right was created, did Congress intend to prevent private suits to enforce the it?

name: Kaiser Aluminum & Chemical Corporation v. Bonjorno
Northbrook National Insurance Company v. Brewer
Grady v. Corbin
question: Does the Double Jeopardy Clause of the Fifth Amendment prevent a person from being charged with more severe offenses after being tried and convicted of lesser ones for the same action?

name: Atlantic Richfield Company v. USA Petroleum Company
question: Must a competitor alleging an "antitrust injury" under the Clayton Act prove predatory intent in addition to showing that the defendant conspired to fix prices in violation of the Sherman Act?

name: Metro Broadcasting, Inc. v. Federal Communications Commission
question: Does the FCC's minority preference policy, giving preference to minority ownership bids for new radio or television broadcasting licenses and permitting "distress sales" to minority owned enterprises only, violate a nonminority bidder's' Fifth Amendment equal protection rights?

name: Commissioner, Immigration and Naturalization Service v. Jean
Osborne v. Ohio
question: Did Ohio's ban on the possession of child pornography violate the First Amendment?

name: General Motors Corporation v. United States
Maryland v. Buie
question: Does the Fourth Amendment prevent police officers from making a “protective sweep” at the site of an in-home arrest if they do not believe themselves or others to be in immediate danger?

name: United States v. Kokinda
question: Is a sidewalk that is entirely contained by Postal Service property and intended only for traffic to and from Postal Service buildings a public forum? If it is a public forum, does a prohibition of solicitation pass strict scrutiny? If it is not a public forum, does it pass a "reasonableness" test?

name: Golden State Transit Corporation v. City of Los Angeles
Commissioner of Internal Revenue v. Indianapolis Power & Light Company
Michigan Department of State Police v. Sitz
question: Did the drunk driving checkpoints violate motorists' privacy protected by the Fourth Amendment?

name: Fort Stewart Schools v. Federal Labor Relations Authority
Milkovich v. Lorain Journal Company
question: Are the statements in the newspaper article constitutionally protected opinions?

name: Department of Treasury, Internal Revenue Service v. Federal Labor Relations Authority
Maislin Industries, US, Inc. v. Primary Steel, Inc.
University of Pennsylvania v. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission
question: Does requiring a university to disclose confidential peer review materials in an investigation violate the First Amendment?

name: New York v. Harris
question: Is the statement of a defendant inadmissible if it is the result of the police entering the defendant’s home without a warrant or consent in violation of the Fourth Amendment?

name: Cruzan by Cruzan v. Director, Missouri Department of Health
question: Did the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment permit Cruzan's parents to refuse life-sustaining treatment on their daughter's behalf?
description: A case in which the Court held that a Missouri state hospital had the right to keep a patient in a vegetative state alive, despite the wishes of the patient's parents, due to a lack of otherwise "clear and convincing" wishes on the part of the patient.

name: Hodgson v. Minnesota
question: Did the Minnesota abortion notification statute unconstitutionally restrict a minor's access to having an abortion?

name: James v. Illinois
question: Could James's statements be used against him even though they were obtained illegally?

name: Citibank, N.A. v. Wells Fargo Asia Ltd.
Danforth v. Minnesota
question: When determining whether Supreme Court decisions on constitutional rules of criminal procedure apply retroactively, may state supreme courts use state-law retroactivity standards that are broader than the standard in Teague v. Lane?

name: Federal Express Corporation v. Holowecki
question: Does an intake questionnaire submitted to the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission qualify as the charge of discrimination required by the Age Discrimination in Employment Act, even if the EEOC did not treat the questionnaire as a charge?
