United States v. Idaho ex rel. Director, Idaho Dept. of Water Resources
Nixon v. United States
question: Is Nixon's claim -- that Senate Rule XI violates the Impeachment Trial Clause -- justiciable, i.e., appropriate for judicial resolution?
description: A case in which the Court held that Senate Rule XI was not subject to judicial review because the "Senate shall have sole Power to try any impeachments."

name: Chisholm v. Georgia
question: Can state citizens sue state governments in federal court?
description: A case in which the Court ruled that the states were under the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and the federal government.

name: Hylton v. United States
question: Was the carriage tax a direct tax, which would require apportionment among the states?
description: A case in which the Court held that the carriage tax was not a direct tax and thus was not subject to apportionment among the states.

name: Ware v. Hylton
question: Does the Treaty of Paris override an otherwise valid state law?
description: A case in which the Court held that federal courts have the power to determine the constitutionality of state laws, and a federal treaty supersedes any conflicting state law under the Supremacy Clause.

name: Calder v. Bull
question: Was the Connecticut legislation a violation of Article 1, Section 10, of the Constitution, which prohibits ex post facto laws?

name: Marbury v. Madison
question:
1. Do the plaintiffs have a right to receive their commissions?
  2. Can they sue for their commissions in court?
  3. Does the Supreme Court have the authority to order the delivery of their commissions?
description: A case in which the Court established a precedent for judicial review in the United States, declaring that acts of Congress that conflict with the Constitution are null and void, as the Constitution is the supreme law of the land.

name: Little v. Barreme
question: Did the President have the authority to issue the order to capture ships travelling from French ports?

name: Fletcher v. Peck
question: Could the contract between Fletcher and Peck be invalidated by an act of the Georgia legislature?
description: A case in which the Court held that a contract is still binding and enforceable, even if secured illegally.

name: New Jersey v. Wilson
question: Did the repeal of the tax exemption impair the obligation of a contract between the state and the new owner of the land?

name: Martin v. Hunter's Lessee
question: Is Section 25 of the Judiciary Act, which grants the U.S. Supreme Court appellate review over state court cases involving federal law, unconstitutional?
description: A case in which the Court ruled that the Supreme Court of the United States overruled the courts of the states.

name: McCulloch v. Maryland
question:
1. Did Congress have the authority to establish the bank?
  2. Did the Maryland law unconstitutionally interfere with congressional powers?
description: A case in which the Court decided that the Second Bank of the United States could not be taxed by the state of Maryland, declaring that the government of individual states cannot impose laws on the functioning of the federal government.

name: Trustees of Dartmouth College v. Woodward
question: Did the New Hampshire legislature unconstitutionally interfere with Dartmouth College's rights under the Contract Clause?
description: A case in which the Court held that the charter to Dartmouth College was a contract between private parties, and that the New Hampshire government's attempt to turn the College into a public institution was unconstitutional under the contract clause.

name: Anderson v. Dunn
question: Does the Congress have the power to punish nonmembers for contempt?

name: Cohens v. Virginia
question: Did the Supreme Court have the power under the Constitution to review the Virginia Supreme Court's ruling?
description: A case in which the Court decided it had jurisdiction over all cases involving Constitutional questions, including state supreme court decisions.

name: Johnson & Graham's Lessee v. McIntosh
question: Can a Native American tribe convey land to individuals?
description: A case in which the Court ruled that Native American nations did not have the right to sell their own land.

name: Gibbons v. Ogden
question: Does the Commerce Clause give Congress authority over interstate navigation?
description: A case in which the Court decided that the federal government has exclusive power over interstate commerce.

name: Osborn v. Bank of the United States
question: Did the federal circuit court's assertion of jurisdiction over the case, which involved an action commenced against the state of Ohio, violate the Eleventh Amendment?

name: Ogden v. Saunders
question: Does a state bankruptcy law applying to contracts made after the law's passage violate the Obligation of Contracts Clause of the Constitution?

name: Willson v. Black Bird Creek Marsh Company
question: Did Delaware's authorization of the building of the dam unconstitutionally infringe upon Congress's powers under the Commerce Clause?

name: Worcester v. Georgia
question: Does the state of Georgia have the authority to regulate the intercourse between citizens of its state and members of the Cherokee Nation?
description: A case in which the Court found that the Georgia legislature lacked the authority to regulate the intercourse between citizens of the state and members of Native American territories.

name: Barron ex rel. Tiernan v. Mayor of Baltimore
question: Does the Fifth Amendment deny the states as well as the national government the right to take private property for public use without justly compensating the property's owner?
description: A case in which the Court found that state governments are not bound by the Fifth Amendment to provide compensation for taking private property.

name: Mayor of New York v. Miln
question: Does the New York law violate the Commerce Clause which vests all power over interstate and foreign commerce in Congress?

name: Briscoe v. Bank of Commonwealth of Kentucky
question: By issuing notes and currency, did the bank violate the constitutional prohibition in Article I Section 10 that "[n]o State shall...emit Bills of Credit"?

name: Proprietors of Charles River Bridge v. Proprietors of Warren Bridge
question: Did the legislature enter into an economic contract with the Charles River Bridge Company that was impaired by the second charter in violation of Article I Section 10 of the Constitution?
description: A case in which the Court held that the Massachusetts legislature did not violate Article I, Section 10 by building a free bridge near a bridge that collected tolls.

name: Groves v. Slaughter
question: Does the Mississippi constitutional provision banning importation and sale of slaves unconstitutionally encroach on congressional commerce power?

name: Prigg v. Pennsylvania
question: Did Pennsylvania's law prohibiting the extradition of Negroes to other states for the purpose of slavery violate Article IV, Section 2 of the Constitution? Did the law violate the Fugitive Slave Law of 1793 as applied by the Supremacy Clause?

name: Jones v. VanZandt
question: Is the Fugitive Slave Law unconstitutional because the Constitution confers to Congress no power over the subject?

name: West River Bridge Company v. Dix
question: Does the taking of the bridge violate the Impairment of Contracts prohibition of Article I Section 10 of the Constitution?

name: Luther v. Borden
question: Did the Court have the constitutional authority to declare which group constituted the official government of Rhode Island?

name: United States v. The Amistad
question: Are the alleged slaves the property of Ruiz and Montez?
description: A case in which the Court held that the alleged slaves that revolted on The Amistad were free Africans and not the property of Spanish citizens.

name: Ewing v. California
question: Did Ewing's sentence of 25 years to life, in accordance with California's three strikes law, violate the Eighth Amendment protection against cruel and unusual punishment?

name: State Farm Mutual Automobile Insurance Company v. Campbell
question: Is an award of $145 million in punitive damages, when full compensatory damages are $1 million, excessive and in violation of the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment?

name: Entergy Louisiana, Inc. v. Louisiana Public Service Commission
question: Does a Federal Energy Regulatory Commission approved tariff that delegates discretion to the regulated entity to determine the precise cost allocation similarly preempt a state order that adjudges those costs imprudent?

name: Kaupp v. Texas
question:
1. Does an arrest for which the police did not obtain a warrant and in which it was not clear that the suspect could decline to go with the police violate the Fourth Amendment?

2. If so, should the subsequent confession be suppressed?
description: A case in which the Court held that an arrest that lacked probable cause and to which the suspect did not consent violated the Fourth Amendment, and therefore any subsequent confession that resulted from the illegal arrest must be suppressed.

name: Demore v. Kim
question: Does the Immigration and Nationality Act, which provides for no-bail, civil detention, violate a lawful permanent resident alien's liberty interest?

name: Nike, Inc. v. Kasky
question: May a corporation participating in a public debate be subjected to liability for factual inaccuracies on the theory that its statements are commercial speech because they might affect consumers' opinions about the business as a good corporate citizen and thereby affect their purchasing decisions?

name: Pierce County v. Guillen
question: Does the Hazard Elimination Program exceed Congress's authority under the Commerce Clause?

name: Breuer v. Jim's Concrete of Brevard, Inc.
question: In providing for suits under the FLSA, did Congress bar removal of such actions from state to federal court?

name: Clay v. United States
question: Does a judgment become "final" for postconviction relief when the appellate court issues its mandate affirming the conviction where a defendant in a federal prosecution takes an unsuccessful direct appeal from a judgment of conviction but does not next petition for a writ of certiorari from the U.S. Supreme Court?

name: Yellow Transportation, Inc. v. Michigan
question: Did the Michigan Supreme Court err in holding that, under the Intermodal Surface Transportation Efficiency Act of 1991, only a State's generic fee is relevant to determining the fee that was collected or charged as of November 15, 1991?

name: Gratz v. Bollinger
question: Did the University of Michigan’s use of racial preferences in undergraduate admissions violate the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment and Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964?
description: A case in which the Court held that the University of Michigan's practice of favoring applicants of certain races in the admissions process violated the Fourteenth Amendment.

name: Virginia v. Black
question: Does the Commonwealth of Virginia's cross-burning statute, which prohibits the burning of a cross with the intent of intimidating any person or group of persons, violate the First Amendment?
description: A case in which the Court held that a law banning cross-burning with the intent to intimidate is constitutional. However, cross burning is not prima facie evidence of intent to intimidate.

name: Archer v. Warner
question: Does the Bankruptcy Code cover a debt embodied in a settlement agreement that settled a creditor's earlier claim "for money...obtained by...fraud?"

name: Federal Communications Commission v. Nextwave Personal Communications, Inc.
question: Does section 525 of the Bankruptcy Code prohibit the Federal Communications Commission from revoking licenses held by a debtor in bankruptcy upon the debtor's failure to make timely payments owed to the FCC for purchase of the licenses?

name: United States v. Bean
question: Does a federal district court, despite appropriation provisions barring the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, and Firearms from acting on applications for relief from firearms disabilities from persons convicted of a felony, have the authority to grant such relief?

name: Beneficial National Bank v. Anderson
question: Does the NBA require that any suits involving charges of excessive interest be heard in federal rather than state court?

name: Virginia v. Hicks
question: Is the Richmond Redevelopment and Housing Authority's trespass policy, which provides for arrest after being served notice for being on the premises without "a legitimate business or social purpose," facially invalid under the First Amendment's overbreadth doctrine?

name: Sell v. United States
question: May the Federal Government administer antipsychotic drugs involuntarily to a mentally ill criminal defendant in order to render that defendant competent to stand trial for serious, but nonviolent, crimes?

name: Meyer v. Holley
question: Does the Fair Housing Act impose personal liability without fault upon an officer or owner of a residential real estate corporation for the unlawful activity of the corporation's employee or agent?

name: Clackamas Gastroenterology Associates, P. C. v. Wells
question: Should four physicians actively engaged in medical practice as shareholders and directors of a professional corporation be counted as employees under the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990?

name: Kentucky Association of Health Plans, Inc. v. Miller
question: Does the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 preempt any of Kentucky's "Any Willing Provider" statutes?

name: Chavez v. Martinez
question: Are a suspect's Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination and his Fourteenth Amendment substantive due process right to be free from coercive questioning violated when he was subjected to coercive questioning while in police custody, even if his coerced statements were never used against him in a criminal case?

name: Early v. Packer
question: Was a state court’s determination that encouraging the jury to continue deliberations did not coerce a verdict?
description: A case in which the Court determined that a trial judge’s encouragement to the jury to continue deliberations did not coerce a verdict.

name: National Park Hospitality Assn. v. Dept. of the Interior
question: Does the Contract Disputes Act of 1978 apply to contracts between the National Park Service and concessioners in the national parks?

name: Miller-El v. Cockrell
question: Must an inmate demonstrate that a state court's finding of the absence of purposeful discrimination was incorrect by clear and convincing evidence in order for a court of appeals to issue a certificate of appealability?

name: Grutter v. Bollinger
question: Does the University of Michigan Law School's use of racial preferences in student admissions violate the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment or Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964?
description: A case in which the Court held that the use of race in the University of Michigan's Law School admissions decisions did not violate the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.

name: Abdur'Rahman v. Bell
question: Does a Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60(b) motion, filed in a habeas corpus proceeding to inform the federal courts of a state court's interpretation of state procedural laws, constitute a "successive" habeas corpus petition?

name: United States v. American Library Assn., Inc.
question: Does Congress have the authority to require libraries to censor internet content in order to receive federal funding?

name: Dow Chemical Company v. Stephenson
question: Does the 1984 Agent Orange settlement preclude plaintiffs, who allege that they were inadequately represented in the prior litigation, from asserting claims?

name: Nguyen v. United States
question: Did a panel of the Court of Appeals consisting of two Article III judges and one Article IV judge have the authority to decide the appeals of two defendants convicted on federal narcotics charges in the District Court of Guam?

name: Borden Ranch Partnership v. Army Corps of Engineers
question: Does deep plowing ranchland to plant deep-rooted crops constitute the "addition" of a "pollutant" from a "point source" so as to fall within the regulation of the Clean Water Act? Is deep plowing ranchland which is farmable in its natural state to plant deep-rooted crops statutorily exempt from regulation under the Act's exemption for any discharge from "normal farming...activities such as plowing?" Does the Act's civil penalty section authorize assessing the maximum daily penalty for each time a plow crosses a seasonal drainage feature, without regard to the number of days when such activity occurred?

name: Brown v. Legal Foundation of Washington
question: Does the use of interest on lawyers' trust accounts to pay for legal services provided to the needy constitute a state taking in violation of the Just Compensation Clause of the Fifth Amendment?

name: Moseley v. V Secret Catalogue, Inc.
question: Does the Federal Trademark Dilution Act require objective proof of actual injury to the economic value of a famous mark for relief?

name: Dastar Corporation v. Twentieth Century Fox Film Corporation
question: Does the Lanham Act prevent the unaccredited copying of a work? If so, may a court double a profit award under the Act in order to deter future infringing conduct?

name: Hillside Dairy, Inc. v. Lyons
question: Does the Federal Agriculture Improvement and Reform Act of 1996 exempt California's milk pricing and pooling regulations from scrutiny under the Commerce Clause? Are individual claims under the Privileges and Immunities Clause against California's required contributions to the price equalization pool on some out-of-state purchases foreclosed because those regulations do not discriminate on their face on the basis of state citizenship or state residence?

name: Cook County v. United States ex rel. Chandler
question: Are local governments "persons" subject to qui tam actions under the False Claims Act?

name: Roell v. Withrow
question: Can consent, under the Federal Magistrate Act of 1979, be inferred from a party's conduct during litigation?

name: Barnhart v. Peabody Coal Company
question: Is the assignment of beneficiaries, under Coal Industry Retiree Health Benefit Act of 1992, valid if the assignment was made after the Act's October 1, 1993 deadline?

name: Boeing Company v. United States
question: Was Boeing Co. required to take into account expenses incurred for R&D in accordance with applicable Treasury regulations in calculating its "combined taxable income" for purposes of determining taxation with respect to its domestic international sales corporation and foreign sales corporation?

name: Bunkley v. Florida
question: Should the first-degree burglary conviction be remanded to the state court to consider whether the inmate’s pocketknife fit within the “common pocketknife” exception at the time his conviction became final?
description: A case in which the Court held that the state court must consider whether an inmate’s pocketknife fit within the “common pocketknife” exception at the time his conviction became final.

name: Immigration and Naturalization Service v. Ventura
question: Should an appellate court remand a case to an agency when additional investigation within the agency’s area of expertise may be required?
description: A case in which the Court held that an appellate court should generally remand a case to an agency when the subject matter is one over which the agency has authority pursuant to a statute.

name: Federal Election Commission v. Beaumont
question: Does the Federal Election Campaign Act's ban on corporate political donations violate the freedom of speech for incorporated, non-profit advocacy groups?

name: Stogner v. California
question: Does the Ex Post Facto Clause bar the application of California's retroactive extension of the statutes of limitations for sexual offenses committed against minors?

name: Fitzgerald v. Racing Association of Central Iowa
question: Do different tax rates levied against racetrack and casino gambling violate the Fourteenth Amendment's Equal Protection Clause?

name: Price  v. Vincent
question: Is a defendant's right against double jeopardy violated when a trial judge grants a motion for a directed verdict of acquittal as to first-degree murder, but does not direct such a verdict to the jury that subsequently convicts the defendant of first-degree murder?

name: Scheidler v. National Organization for Women, Inc.
question: Do abortion opponents, who protest at abortion clinics, commit extortion within the meaning of the Hobbs Act? May abortion supporters obtain injunctive relief in a civil action pursuant to the Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act?

name: United States v. White Mt. Apache Tribe
question: Does the Court of Federal Claims, under the Indian Tucker Act, have jurisdiction over the White Mountain Apache Tribe's suit against the United States for breach of fiduciary duty to manage land and improvements held in trust for the Tribe but occupied by the federal government?

name: Jinks v. Richland County, South Carolina
question: Is 28 USC section 1367(d), which requires state statute of limitations to be tolled for the period during which a plaintiff's cause of action had previously been pending in federal court, constitutional as applied to lawsuits brought against a State's political subdivisions?

name: Los Angeles v. David
question: Does a 27-day delay before a hearing violate the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment by denying an individual the opportunity to be heard “at a meaningful time and in an meaningful manner”?
description: A case in which the Court held that a 27-day wait for a hearing disputing a parking ticket did not violate the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.

name: Eldred v. Ashcroft
question: Does the 1998 Copyright Term Extension Act's extension of existing copyrights exceed Congress's power under the Copyright Clause? Does the CTEA's extension of existing and future copyrights violate the First Amendment?

name: Ford Motor Company v. Romo
question: Is an award of $290 million in punitive damages, when full compensatory damages are $5 million, excessive and in violation of the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment?

name: Medical Board of California v. Hason
question: Does the 11th Amendment's grant of sovereign immunity bar suit under Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act for denial of a medical license based on an applicant's mental illness?

name: American Insurance Ass'n v. Garamendi
question: Did California's passage of the HVIRA interfere with the federal government's sovereignty over foreign affairs established by Article I of the Constitution?

name: Woodford v. Visciotti
question: Was a state court’s application of the Supreme Court’s ineffective assistance of counsel precedent as requiring the defendant to show prejudice by a preponderance of the evidence objectively unreasonable?
description: A case in which the Court determined that a federal court cannot reverse a state court’s decision on habeas review when the state court reasonably applied precedent requiring the defendant show prejudice by strong evidence of ineffective counsel.

name: Lockyer v. Andrade
question: Did the Federal Court of Appeals err in holding that California Court of Appeal's affirmation of a sentence of two consecutive terms of 25 years to life in prison for a "third strike" conviction was "grossly disproportionate" to the crime and thus violated the Eighth Amendment's prohibition on "cruel and unusual punishment"?

name: PacifiCare Health Systems, Inc. v. Book
question: Can a group of physicians be compelled to arbitrate claims arising under the Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act, even though the parties' arbitration agreements may be construed to limit the arbitrator's authority to award damages?

name: Franchise Tax Board of California v. Hyatt
question: Does the Nevada Supreme Court's refusal to extend full faith and credit to California's statute immunizing its tax collection agency from suit violate the Full Faith and Credit Clause of the Constitution?

name: Wiggins v. Smith
question: Does a criminal defendant's attorneys' failure to investigate his background and present mitigating evidence of his unfortunate life history at his capital sentencing proceedings constitute ineffective assistance of counsel?

name: United States v. Navajo Nation
question: Can the U.S. be held liable for a breach of trust with an Indian Tribe in connection with the negotiation of a mining lease, even when the U.S. has violated no specific statutory or regulatory duty established in the Indian Mineral Leasing Act of 1938?

name: United States v. Jimenez Recio
question: Is the Ninth Circuit rule -- that a conspiracy ends automatically when the object of the conspiracy becomes impossible to achieve -- valid?

name: Black & Decker Disability Plan v. Nord
question: Under ERISA, are companies required to defer to the decision of a disability claimant's personal physician?

name: Massaro v. United States
question: Must claims of ineffective assistance of counsel, whether or not there is new counsel on appeal and whether or not the basis for the claim is apparent from the trial record, be raised on direct appeal?

name: Sprietsma v. Mercury Marine
question: Does the Federal Boat Safety Act of 1971 preempt state common-law claims related to propeller safety?

name: Illinois ex rel. Madigan v. Telemarketing Associates, Inc.
question: Does the First Amendment permit a State to maintain fraud actions alleging that fundraisers made false or misleading representations designed to deceive donors about how their donations will be used?

name: Sattazahn v. Pennsylvania
question: Does either the Fifth Amendment's Double Jeopardy Clause or the Fourteenth Amendment's Due Process Clause bar a state from seeking the death penalty upon retrial where a statutory life sentence for murder was imposed after the jury was unable to agree on a sentence?

name: Norfolk & Western Railway Company v. Ayers
question: Can an employer be held liable for pain and suffering caused by a disease that has not yet been contracted? And are railroad companies liable for full damages under FELA even if the actions or negligence of other parties contributed to the damage inflicted?

name: Georgia v. Ashcroft
question: Did the redistricting plan violate the Voting Rights Act of 1965 by spreading minority voters across several districts rather than concentrating them in a few heavily minority ones?

name: Connecticut Department of Public Safety v. Doe
question: Does the Fourteenth Amendment's Due Process Clause require that persons convicted of sexual offenses subject to Connecticut's "Megan's Law" receive a hearing before the public disclosure of their registry?

name: Woodford v. Garceau
question: Is a federal habeas petition, which was filed after the effective date of the Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act of 1996 even though a stay and counsel were sought prior to that date, "pending" for the purposes of Lindh v. Murphy, 521 U.S. 320?

name: Nevada Department of Human Resources v. Hibbs
question: May an individual sue a State for money damages in federal court for violation of the Family and Medical Leave Act of 1993?

name: Desert Palace, Inc. v. Costa
question: Must a plaintiff present direct evidence of discrimination in order to obtain a mixed-motive instruction under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 as amended by the Civil Rights Act of 1991?

name: Washington State Department of Health and Human Services v. Guardianship Estate of Keffeler
question: Does the State of Washington's use of foster childrens' Social Security benefits to reimburse itself for some of its expenditures violate the provision of the Social Security Act that protects benefits from "execution, levy, attachment, garnishment, or other legal process?"

name: Pharmaceutical Research & Manufacturers of America v. Walsh
question: Is a Maine statute providing for affordable prescription drugs pre-empted by the Supremacy Clause? Does the statute violate the Commerce Clause?

name: Inyo County v. Paiute-Shoshone Indians
question: Does a federally recognized tribe qualify as a "person" who may sue under 42 USC section 1983? Does a tribe's suit qualify for federal-court jurisdiction because it arises under some federal law other than section 1983?

name: Green Tree Financial Corp. v. Bazzle
question: Does the Federal Arbitration Act permit class-wide arbitration hearings?

name: Lawrence v. Texas
question: Do the criminal convictions of John Lawrence and Tyron Garner under the Texas "Homosexual Conduct" law, which criminalizes sexual intimacy by same-sex couples, but not identical behavior by different-sex couples, violate the Fourteenth Amendment guarantee of equal protection of laws? Do their criminal convictions for adult consensual sexual intimacy in the home violate their vital interests in liberty and privacy protected by the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment? Should Bowers v. Hardwick, 478 U.S. 186 (1986), be overruled?
description: A case in which the Court found that a Texas statute banning consenting homosexual adults from engaging in sexual acts violated the Fourteenth Amendment's guarantee of equal protection.

name: Dole Food Company v. Patrickson
question: May a corporate subsidiary claim instrumentality status where the foreign state does not own a majority of its shares but does own a majority of the shares of a corporate parent one or more tiers above the subsidiary? Is a corporation's instrumentality status defined as of the time an alleged tort or other actionable wrong occurred?

name: Citizens Bank v. Alafabco, Inc.
question: Is a debt-restructuring agreement between two parties a transaction that substantially involves interstate commerce so that the Federal Arbitration Act may apply?
description: A case in which the Court held that the parties’ debt-restructuring agreement affected interstate commerce, and therefore their arbitration clause was enforceable under the Federal Arbitration Act.

name: Syngenta Crop Protection, Inc. v. Henson
question: Does the All Writs Act give a federal district court the authority to remove a state-court case in order to prevent the frustration of orders the federal court has previously issued?

name: Howsam v. Dean Witter Reynolds, Inc.
question: Should a federal district court decide whether to interpret and apply the National Association of Securities Dealers' time-limit rule regarding disputes where six years have elapsed since the event that gives rise to the dispute?

name: Ford Motor Co. v. McCauley
question: Is the amount-in-controversy requirement of the federal diversity statute satisfied where a class representative seeks an injunction that would cost the defendant more than $75,000 to implement whether the injunction applies to one plaintiff or all class members?

name: Smith v. Doe
question: Does the Ex Post Facto Clause of Article I Section 10 prohibit the Alaska Sex Offender Registration Act's registration requirement as a retroactive punishment?

name: Overton v. Bazzetta
question: Did the Department of Corrections ban on visits by minors violate the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment, the Cruel and Unusual Punishment Clause of the Eighth Amendment and the freedom of association of the First Amendment?

name: City of Cuyahoga Falls v. Buckeye Community Hope
question: Did the Court of Appeals err in holding that a low-income housing foundation's suit against a city for violations of the Equal Protection and Due Process Clauses of the Fourteenth Amendment and the Fair Housing Act could proceed to trial?

name: Branch v. Smith
question: Did the District Court properly enjoin the Mississippi state court's proposed congressional redistricting plan and properly fashion its own congressional reapportionment plan?

name: Scales v. United States
question: Does a Communist Party member's conviction under the Smith Act, which makes a felony the knowing membership in organizations advocating the violent or forceful overthrow of the United States government, violate the Fifth Amendment's due process clause in light of the apparent protections afforded to such members under the Internal Security Act?
description: Scales was prosecuted and convicted of a felony for his membership in the Communist Party, which advocated the violent overthrow of the government, and was illegal under the Smith Act.

name: Gallagher v. Crown Kosher Super Market of Massachusetts, Inc.
question: Do statutes that require stores to close on Sundays violate the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment by not respecting the establishment of religion and prohibiting free exercise as applied to the states?
description: A case in which the Court held that statutes requiring stores to stay closed on Sundays do not violate the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment

name: Communist Party of the United States v. Subversive Activities Control Board
Laurens Federal Savings & Loan Assn. v. South Carolina Tax Commission
Meyer v. United States
question: Can a federal tax lien attach to the net proceeds of life insurance policies paid to Peter Meyer's widow?

name: Jarecki v. G. D. Searle & Company
Burton v. Wilmington Parking Authority
question: Did the Eagle Coffee Shoppe's refusal to serve Burton constitute a violation of the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment?

name: United States v. John Hancock Mutual Life Insurance Company
Maynard v. Durham & Southern Railway Company
Eli Lilly & Company v. Sav-on-Drugs, Inc.
Aro Manufacturing Company, Inc. v. Convertible Top Replacement Company, Inc.
question: Can a patent holder prevent the manufacture and/or distribution of a replacement part for a patented device when the replacement part is not itself patented?

name: Moses Lake Homes, Inc. v. Grant County
Schnell v. Peter Eckrich & Sons, Inc.
Chaunt v. United States
question: Did the Government meet its standard of proof required under the Immigration and Nationality Act to revoke an order of naturalization?
description: A case in which the Court the Government did not meet its standard of proof required under the Immigration and Nationality Act to revoke an order of naturalization.

name: Marcus v. Search Warrant of Property at 104 East Tenth Street, Kansas City, Missouri
Knetsch v. United States
question: Did the transaction between Knetsch and the insurance company create an indebtedness within the meaning of the Internal Revenue Code?

name: Mapp v. Ohio
question: Were the confiscated materials protected from seizure by the Fourth Amendment?
description: A case in which the Court decided that evidence obtained illegally may not be used against someone in a court of law by the Fourth Amendment.

name: Bulova Watch Company, Inc. v. United States
H. K. Porter Company, Inc. v. Central Vermont Railway, Inc.
United States v. Mississippi Valley Generating Company
Goldberg v. Whitaker House Cooperative, Inc.
Konigsberg v. State Bar of California
International Ladies' Garment Workers' Union, AFL-CIO v. National Labor Relations Board
American Automobile Association v. United States
Louisiana ex rel. Gremillion v. NAACP
Chicago, Milwaukee, St. Paul & Pacific Railroad Co v. United States
Power Reactor Development Company v. International Union of Electrical, Radio and Machine Workers, AFL-CIO
Gomillion v. Lightfoot
question: Did the redrawing of Tuskegee's electoral district boundaries violate the Fifteenth Amendment?

name: Local 761, International Union of Electrical, Radio & Machine Workers, AFL-CIO v. National Labor Relations Board
Dayton Rubber Co. v. Cordovan Associates, Inc.
National Labor Relations Board v. News Syndicate Company, Inc.
Times Film Corporation v. City of Chicago
International typographical Union, AFL-CIO v. National Labor Relations Board
Waterman Steamship Corporation v. Dugan & McNamara, Inc.
United States v. Consolidated Edison Company of New York, Inc.
Two Guys from Harrison-Allentown, Inc. v. McGinley
Wilkinson v. United States
question:
(1) Were the questions asked of Wilkinson pertinent to the subjects under inquiry?

(2) Did the subcommittee have the authority to question Wilkinson?

name: Torcaso v. Watkins
question: Does a state requirement that a candidate for public office profess a belief in God in order to be eligible violate the First Amendment protection of the freedom of religion?

name: New York, New Haven & Hartford Railroad Company v. Henagan
Monroe v. Pape
question:
1. Does a person have a valid cause of action under the Civil Rights Act against police officers when the police officers violate that person's due process?

2. Can municipalities be liable under the Civil Rights Act?

name: Federal Power Commission v. Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Corporation
Horton v. Liberty Mutual Insurance Company
United States v. Virginia Electric & Power Company
question: Does land used for easement have compensable value when appropriated by the government?

name: Civil Aeronautics Board v. Delta Air Lines, Inc.
Communist Party, U. S. A. v. Catherwood
Eastern Railroad Presidents Conference v. Noerr Motor Freight, Inc.
Binks Mfg. Co. v. Ransburg Electro-Coating Corp.
United States v. Parke, Davis & Company
United States v. E.I. du Pont de Nemours & Company
Sam Fox Publishing Company, Inc. v. United States
Baker v. Carr
question: Did the Supreme Court have jurisdiction over questions of legislative apportionment?
description: A case in which the Court found that redistricting issues present justiciable questions, and in which the Court reframed its political question doctrine.

name: Poe v. Ullman
question: Did the Connecticut law violate liberty protected by due process of the Fourteenth Amendment?
description: A case in which the Court held that the ripeness doctrine prevents bringing claims to challenge criminal statutes that are not enforced.

name: Local 357, International Brotherhood of Teamsters, Chauffeurs, Warehousemen and Helpers of America v. National Labor Relations Board
Braunfeld v. Brown
question: Did the Pennsylvania blue law violate the First Amendment's protection of free exercise of religious beliefs?

name: Local 60, United Brotherhood of Carpenters and Joiners of America, AFL-CIO v. National Labor Relations Board
Brotherhood of Maintenance of Way Employees v. United States
National Labor Relations Board v. Radio and Television Broadcast Engineers Union, Local 1212, International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, AFL-CIO
Boynton v. Virginia
question: Did Boyton’s conviction violate the Interstate Commerce Act?
description: A case in which the Court held that the conviction of an interstate bus passenger for refusing to leave the premises of a segregated restaurant violated the Interstate Commerce Act.

name: Radiant Burners, Inc. v. Peoples Gas Light & Coke Company
National Labor Relations Board v. Mattison Machine Works
McGowan v. Maryland
question: Do Maryland's blue laws violate the Free Exercise and Religious Establishment clauses of the First Amendment?

name: Pan American Petroleum Corporation v. Superior Court of Delaware for New Castle County
Tampa Electric Company v. Nashville Coal Company
Lewis v. Manufacturers National Bank of Detroit
Wooley v. Maynard
question: Did the New Hampshire law unconstitutionally interfere with the freedom of speech guaranteed by the First Amendment?

name: Milliken v. Bradley
question:
(1) Can a federal district court order remedial education programs for students who had been subjected to segregation?

(2) Can a federal district court order the state of Michigan to bear some of the costs of the remedial programs without violating Michigan's immunity from suit established by the Eleventh Amendment?

name: United States v. County of Fresno
Nixon v. Administrator of General Services
question:
1. Was the Presidential Recordings and Materials Preservation Act unconstitutional on its face as a violation of the separation of powers?

2. Was the act unconstitutional on its face as a violation of presidential privilege doctrines?

3. Was the act unconstitutional on its face as a violation of Nixon’s privacy interests?

4. Was the act unconstitutional on its face as a violation of Nixon’s First Amendment right to free association?

5. Was the act unconstitutional on its face as a violation of the Bill of Attainder Clause?

name: Trans World Airlines, Inc. v. Hardison
Moore v. City of East Cleveland
question: Did the housing ordinance violate the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment?

name: United States v. Board of Supervisors of Warren County, Mississippi
United States v. Antelope
question: Do federal criminal statutes that subject individuals to federal prosecution based on their status as American Indians violate the Due Process Clause of the Fifth Amendment?

name: United States v. Consumer Life Insurance Company
Bounds v. Smith
question: Did the First and Fourteenth Amendments require the North Carolina Department of Corrections to assist inmates in the preparation and filing of legal papers by providing adequate law libraries or adequate legal assistance?

name: Oregon v. Mathiason
question: Can incriminating evidence obtained from a suspect during a voluntary interview be used if the police did not read Miranda rights to the suspect?

name: Donovan v. Penn Shipping Company, Inc.
Delaware Tribal Business Committee v. Weeks
Concerned Citizens of Southern Ohio, Inc. v. Pine Creek Conservancy District
Dothard v. Rawlinson
question:
(1) Do the height and weight requirements violate Title VII?

(2) Does the ban on women in “contact positions” violate Title VII?

name: Brunswick Corporation v. Pueblo Bowl-O-Mat, Inc.
Poelker v. Doe
question: Did the policy violate the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment?

name: City of Philadelphia v. New Jersey
question:
(1) Does the Solid Waste Disposal Act of 1965 pre-empt the New Jersey statute?

(2) Does the New Jersey's statute violate the Commerce Clause of Article I of the Constitution?

name: Coker v. Georgia
question: Was the imposition of the death penalty for the crime of rape a form of cruel and unusual punishment forbidden by the Eighth Amendment?
description: A case in which the Court ruled that use of the capital punishment as a penalty for rape was a form of cruel and unusual punishment forbidden by the Eighth Amendment.

name: United Air Lines, Inc. v. Evans
Bates v. State Bar of Arizona
question: Did the Arizona rule, which restricted legal advertising, violate the freedom of speech of Bates and his firm as guaranteed by the First and Fourteenth Amendments?

name: Beal v. Doe
question: Did Title XIX of the Social Security Act require states that participate in the Medicaid program to fund the cost of nontherapeutic abortions?

name: Hunt v. Washington State Apple Advertising Commission
question: Did the North Carolina regulation violate the Commerce Clause by placing an unreasonable burden on interstate commerce?

name: Northeast Marine Terminal Company, Inc. v. Caputo
Linmark Associates, Inc. v. Township of Willingboro
Jones v. North Carolina Prisoners' Labor Union, Inc.
National Geographic Society v. California Board of Equalization
Boston Stock Exchange v. State Tax Commission
Hazelwood School District v. United States
question:
Does congress have the authority to prohibit racial discrimination under Title VII absent proof that a governmental agency purposely discriminated on the basis of race?

Can a court rely on statistical evidence to find prima facie case of race discrimination?

name: Continental T. V., Inc. v. GTE Sylvania Inc.
question: Is a per se rule barring a manufacturer from restricting the locations where retailers can sell the manufacturer’s products the appropriate rule to evaluate location restrictions?
description: A case in which the Court held that a reasonableness standard is the appropriate standard to apply when evaluating whether a manufacturer’s location restrictions violate Sherman Anti-Trust Act.

name: G. M. Leasing Corporation v. United States
Nolde Brothers, Inc. v. Local No. 358, Bakery & Confectionary Workers Union, AFL-CIO
Brewer v. Williams
question:
(1) Was Williams denied counsel in violation of the Sixth Amendment?

(2) Did Williams waive his right to counsel when he led the detective to the girl’s body?

name: Zacchini v. Scripps-Howard Broadcasting Company
question: Do the First and Fourteenth Amendments immunize the Scripps-Howard Broadcasting Co. from damages for its alleged infringement of an entertainer's state-law right of publicity?

name: Maher v. Roe
question: Did the Connecticut law violate the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment?

name: City of Madison Joint School District No. 8 v. Wisconsin Employment Relations Commission
Oklahoma Publishing Company v. District Court in and for Oklahoma County, Oklahoma
United States v. Lovasco
question: By indicting Lovasco for crimes he allegedly committed 18 months prior, did the government violate either: (1) the defendant’s Sixth Amendment right to a speedy trial or (2) his due process rights guaranteed by the Fifth Amendment?
description: A case in which the Court held that the Sixth Amendment right to a speedy trial applies only after a person has been accused of a crime and that the pre-indictment delay did not deprive Lovasco of due process, though the lapse of time somewhat prejudiced his defense.

name: Whalen v. Roe
question: Did the reporting and record-keeping requirements violate the constitutional right to privacy embraced by the concept of liberty under the Fourteenth Amendment?

name: Santa Fe Industries, Inc. v. Green
Complete Auto Transit Inc. v. Brady
question: Did the Mississippi tax violate the Commerce Clause because it placed a burden on an activity associated with interstate commerce?

name: National Socialist Party of America v. Village of Skokie
question: Did the Illinois Supreme Court improperly deny the National Socialist Party's request for a stay of the district court's injunction?
description: A case in which the Court decided the Illinois Supreme Court improperly denied a stay for an injunction which violated the National Socialist party of its First Amendment rights.

name: Abood v. Detroit Board of Education
Commissioner v. Standard Life & Accident Ins. Company
Vorchheimer v. School Dist. of Philadelphia
E. I. du Pont de Nemours & Company v. Train
question:
(1) Can the EPA issue industry-wide regulations that categorically limit the amount of pollutants that existing manufacturing plants can discharge?

(2) Does the Court of Appeals have jurisdiction to review the EPA regulations that apply to existing plants?

(3) Can the EPA subject newly constructed manufacturing plants to exacting pollution standards that do not allow for any variance from the prescribed limit?
description: A case in which the Court held that the Environmental Protection Agency could place categorical pollution limits on existing manufacturing plants while also placing absolute pollution limits on newly constructed manufacturing plants.

name: Chappelle v. Greater Baton Rouge Airport District
Atlas Roofing Company, Inc. v. Occupational Safety and Health Commission
Ingraham v. Wright
question: Does the cruel and unusual punishment clause of the Eighth Amendment forbid corporal punishment inflicted by teachers and administrators upon Ingraham and Andrews at Charles R. Drew Junior High School? Does Dade County School System’s corporal punishment policy violate due process?

name: Califano v. Goldfarb
question: Do the gender-based requirements for survivor's benefits in Section 402 violate the Due Process Clause of the Fifth Amendment?

name: Oregon ex rel. State Land Bd. v. Corvallis Sand & Gravel Company
National Labor Relations Board v. Enterprise Association of Steam, Hot Water, Hydraulic Sprinkler, Pneumatic Tube, Ice Machine & General Pipefitters of New York and Vicinity, Local Union No. 638
Standard Oil Company of California v. United States
Local 3489, United Steelworkers of America, AFL-CIO v. Usery
Smith v. Organization of Foster Families For Equality & Reform
Trimble v. Gordon
question: Did Section 12 of the Illinois Probate Act violate the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment?

name: East Texas Motor Freight System, Inc. v. Rodriguez
School District of Omaha v. United States
Don E. Williams Company v. Commissioner of Internal Revenue
Village of Arlington Heights v. Metropolitan Housing Development Corporation
question: Was Arlington Height's denial of a zoning request, necessary for the creation of low-and moderate-income housing, racially discriminatory in violation of the Fourteenth Amendment's Equal Protection Clause?

name: Ohio Bureau of Employment Services v. Hodory
Occidental Life Insurance Company of California v. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission
Puyallup Tribe, Inc. v. Department of Game of Washington
Idaho ex rel. Andrus v. Oregon
International Union of Electrical, Radio & Machine Workers, AFL-CIO, Local 790 v. Robbins & Myers, Inc.
Gravitt v. Southwestern Bell Telephone Company
Stencel Aero Engineering Corporation v. United States
Town of Lockport v. Citizens for Community Action at the Local Level, Inc.
E. I. du Pont de Nemours & Company v. Collins
United Jewish Organizations of Williamsburgh, Inc. v. Carey
question: Did the reapportionment plan violate the Fourteenth and Fifteenth Amendment rights of the Hasidic community?

name: United States Steel Corporation v. Fortner Enterprises, Inc.
Ward v. Illinois
question: Is the Illinois obscenity statute unconstitutionally vague and/or overbroad?
description: A case in which the Court held that the Illinois obscenity statute was not unconstitutionally vague or overbroad.

name: Dobbert v. Florida
question: Did the changes to the Florida death penalty statutes submit Dobbert to a trial by ex post facto laws or deny him his rights to equal protection and a fair trial?

name: United States Trust Company of New York v. New Jersey
question: In repealing the 1962 agreement, did the states violate the Contract Clause?

name: Estelle v. Gamble
question:
1. Did Gamble’s pro se complaint that the Walls unit subjected him to cruel and unusual punishment raise a constitutional question or state a claim upon which relief can be granted?

2. Did the Fifth Circuit err in reversing the district court’s summary dismissal of Gamble’s complaint because the complaint rested on a disagreement between licensed physicians about Gamble’s injury?

name: Manson v. Brathwaite
question: Did the court of appeals err in allowing the police officer to identify Brathwaite from a single photograph?

name: Craig v. Boren
question: Did an Oklahoma statute violate the Fourteenth Amendment's Equal Protection Clause by establishing different drinking ages for men and women?
description: A case in which the Court decided that having different ages at which men and women can drink alcoholic beverages was against the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.

name: Bayside Enterprises, Inc. v. National Labor Relations Board
United States v. Martin Linen Supply Company
Third National Bank in Nashville v. Impac Limited, Inc.
Dayton Board of Education v. Brinkman
Mt. Healthy City Bd. of Ed. v. Doyle
question:
1. Was Mt. Healthy City School District Board protected by the sovereign immunity clause of the Eleventh Amendment?

2. Was Mt. Healthy City School District Board forbidden by the First Amendment from considering Doyle’s phone call to a radio station in its decision not to renew Doyle’s contract?

name: FAA v. Cooper
question: Does the Privacy Act's "actual damages" provision cover mental and emotional distress?
description: A case in which the Court held that the Privacy Act of 1974 does not cover mental and emotional distress under "actual damages."

name: Lafler v. Cooper
question: Is a state habeas petitioner entitled to relief when his counsel deficiently advises him to reject a favorable plea bargain but the defendant is later convicted and sentenced pursuant to a fair trial?
description: A case in which the Court found that the test to determine ineffective assistance of counsel, from Strickland v. Washington, was not properly applied in an aggravated assault case.

name: FCC v. Fox Television Stations
question: Did the court of appeals err in finding the FCC's indecency policy unconstitutionally vague in its entirety?
description: A case in which the Court determined that an FCC policy regarding profane language was too vague, and which was remanded to the Second Circuit Court of Appeals to determine if the FCC violated its customers' First Amendment rights.

name: Salazar v. Ramah Navajo Chapter
question: Under the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act, is the government required to pay all of the contract support costs incurred by a tribal contractor, as mandated by the Act, if payment of those costs would exceed the express statutory cap on the appropriations available to pay such costs?
description: A case in which the Court held that, under the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act, the government is required to pay all of the contract support costs incurred by a tribal contractor if payment of those costs would exceed the statutory cap on the appropriations available to pay them.

name: Vasquez v. United States
question: Did the court apply the correct test in determining that the introduction of conversations between Marina Perez and her husband into evidence was a harmless error? If so, did this error violate Vasquez's Sixth Amendment right to a trial by jury?
description: A case which the Court dismissed regarding whether or not the Seventh Circuit violated Supreme Court precedent on harmless error by focusing its analysis solely on the weight of untainted evidence, without considering any potential effects of the error.

name: Hosanna-Tabor Evangelical Lutheran Church and School v. EEOC
question: Does the ministerial exception, which prohibits most employment-related lawsuits against religious organizations by employees performing religious functions, apply to a teacher at a religious elementary school who teaches the full secular curriculum, but also teaches daily religion classes, is a commissioned minister, and regularly leads students in prayer and worship?
description: A case in which the Court found that a woman employed by a religious school who taught daily religion classes, was a commissioned minister, and regularly lead students in prayer and worship, did not have grounds to sue the school under the Ministerial Exception.

name: Vartelas v. Holder
question: Can 8 U.S.C. § 1101(a)(13)(C)(v) be applied retroactively to a Lawful Permanent Resident who pleads guilty to a crime of moral turpitude prior to the effective date of the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act?
description: A case in which the Court held that 8 U.S.C. § 1101(a)(13)(C)(v) cannot be applied retroactively to a lawful permanent resident who pleads guilty to a crime prior to the effective date of the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act.

name: Christopher v. SmithKline
question:
1. Must Glaxo and the courts defer to the Secretary of Labor's definition of "outside salesman" under the Fair Labor Standards Act?

2. Does the Secretary of Labor's definition of "outside salesman" apply to pharmaceutical sales representatives?
description: A case in which the Court held that the Secretary of Labor's definition of "outside salesman" apply to pharmaceutical sales representatives under the Fair Labor Standards Act.

name: KPMG LLP v. Cocchi
question: Does a court have a duty under the Federal Arbitration Act (FAA) to compel arbitration of a complaint where some claims are not arbitrable?
description: A case in which the Court held that, under the Federal Arbitration Act, a court must allow arbitration for those claims that are arbitrable, even if other claims are not.

name: United States v. Home Concrete & Supply
question:
1. Can an understatement of gross income attributable to an overstatement of basis in sold property qualify as an "omi[ssion] from gross income" that triggers the extended six-year assessment period?

2. Is a final regulation from the Department of the Treasury reflecting the IRS's view that an understatement of gross income attributable to an overstatement of basis which can trigger the extended six-year assessment period entitled to judicial deference?
description: A case in which the Court held that section 6501(e)(1)(A) of the Internal Revenue Code does not apply when a taxpayer overstates the amount of property that he has sold, which then understates the gain received from the sale.

name: Ryburn v. Huff
question: Did the police officers violate the Fourth Amendment by entering a home without a warrant when the homeowner exhibited unusual behavior leading the officers to believe they were in danger?
description: A case in which the Court held that police officers did not violate a homeowner's Fourth Amendment rights when they entered the home without a warrant after observing the homeowner exhibiting unusual behavior that led to their belief the homeowner was in danger.

name: Zivotofsky v. Clinton
question: Does the political question doctrine deprive a federal court of jurisdiction to enforce a federal statute that explicitly directs the Secretary of State how to record the birthplace of an American citizen on a Consular Report of Birth Abroad and on a passport?
description: A case in which the Court held that a dispute over passport regulation was not a political issue and is thus liable for judicial review.

name: Sackett v. EPA
question: Do landowners have a right to go to court to challenge a Clean Water Act order of the Environmental Protection Agency?
description: A case in which the Court found that homeowners have a right to go to court over a Clean Water Act order of the Environmental Protection Agency.

name: Pacific Operators Offshore v. Valladolid
question: The Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act extends workers' compensation coverage under the Longshore and Harbor Workers' Compensation Act "with respect to disability or death of an employee resulting from any injury occurring as the result of operations conducted on the outer Continental Shelf for the purpose of exploring for, developing, removing, or transporting by pipeline the natural resources of the outer Continental Shelf." Does the OCSLA extend Longshore Act coverage only to workers injured on the outer Continental Shelf itself?
description: A case in which the Court held that the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act extends coverage for injuries that occurred as the result of operations conducted on the outer continental shelf to an employee, as long as the employee can establish a substantial connection between the injury and the employer’s extractive operations.

name: RadLAX Gateway Hotel v. Amalgamated Bank
question: Under the bankruptcy code, may RadLAX pursue a Chapter 11 bankruptcy plan which proposes to sell assets free of liens, without allowing Amalgamated Bank to bid on credit, but instead providing the creditor with the equivalent of its claim?
description: A case in which the Court held that a company could not obtain confirmation of a Chapter 11 bankruptcy plan that provided for the sale of its assets free from lien without permitting a bank to credit-bid at the sale.

name: Perry v. Perez
question: Did the district court abuse its discretion under the Voting Rights Act when it redrew 36 electoral districts?
description: A case which the Court remanded regarding whether or not a Texas district court abused its discretion under the Voting Rights Act when it redrew 36 districts.

name: United States v. Alvarez
question: Does 18 U.S.C. 704(b), the Stolen Valor Act, violate the Free Speech Clause of the First Amendment?
description: A case in which the Court found that the Stolen Valor Act violated the First Amendment.

name: Freeman v. Quicken Loans, Inc.
question: Does Section 8(b) of the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act prohibit a real estate settlement services provider from charging an unearned fee only if the fee is divided between two or more parties?
description: A case in which the Court held that Section 8(b) of the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act prohibits a real estate service provider from charging an unearned fee if the fee is divided between two or more parties.

name: Marmet Health Care Center v. Brown
question: Did the state court err when it held that the arbitration clauses were invalid due to public policy?
description: A case in which the Court held that a Virginia court incorrectly applied provisions of the FAA regarding nursing homes and personal injury/death disputes.

name: Smith v. Cain
question:
Was there a reasonable probability that the outcome would have been different if the undisclosed witness statements were presented at trial?

Did the State of Louisiana ignore due process by rejecting Smith's Brady claim?
description: A case in which the Court held that the omission of eyewitness testimony in a murder trial, which was the only evidence linking the accused to the crime, was a violation of the accused's due process.

name: Armour v. City of Indianapolis
question: Did the City of Indianapolis violate equal protection by forgiving only outstanding Barrett Law assessment balances, and not those of property owners who paid in full?
description: A case in which the Court held that an Indiana town did not violate residents' Fourteenth Amendment rights when it denied them reimbursement for paying property assessment fees, later deemed to be more than necessary, in full.

name: Astrue v. Capato
question: Are Karen K. Capato's twins - conceived by in vitro fertilization after their biological father's death - "child(ren)" under Title II of the Social Security Act?
description: A case in which the Court held that twins, born through in vitro fertilization after the death of their biological father, were not "children" under Title II of the Social Security act.

name: Howes v. Fields
question: Does federal law automatically require Miranda warnings before questioning jail or prison inmates about issues unrelated to the cases for which they were incarcerated?
description: A case in which the Court held that a prisoner, currently held in jail, did not have his Miranda rights violated when he was questioned inside the jail for a different crime.

name: National Federation of Independent Business v. Sebelius
question:
1. Is the suit brought by respondents to challenge the minimum coverage provision of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act barred by the Anti-Injunction Act, 2 U.S.C. 7421(a)?
  2. Does Congress have power under Article I, Section 8 of the Constitution, specifically under the Commerce Clause or the Taxing and Spending Clause, to require most Americans to purchase health insurance?
  3. Is the individual mandate severable from the ACA?
  4. Did Congress exceed its enumerated powers and violate principles of federalism when it pressured States into accepting conditions that Congress could not impose directly by threatening to withhold all federal funding under Medicaid, the single largest grant-in-aid program?
description: Cases in which the Court held that the minimum coverage requirement of the Affordable Care Act was constitutional, that Congress had the power to enforce the taxation of most Americans that did not buy the minimum level of coverage, and that the federal government exceeded its power by pressuring States into accepting conditions that Congress could not impose directly by threatening to withhold all federal funding under Medicaid.

name: PPL Montana v. Montana
question: Does the constitutional test for determining whether a section of a river is navigable for title purposes require a trial court to determine whether the relevant stretch of the river was navigable at the time of statehood?
description: A case in which the Court held that the constitutional test for determining whether a section of a river is navigable for title purposes requires a trial court to determine whether the relevant stretch of the river was navigable at the time of statehood.

name: Kawashima v. Holder
question: Is filing a false statement on a corporate tax return an aggravated felony involving fraud or deceit, which would render the immigrant removable?
description: A case in which the Court held that filing a false tax return in violation of 26 U.S.C. Section 7206 qualifies as an aggravated felony under the Immigration and Nationality Act if the Government's revenue loss exceeds $10,000.

name: Tennant v. Jefferson County Commission
question: Does the population disparity in West Virginia's apportionment of voting districts violate Article I Section 2 of the U.S. Constitution?
description: A case in which the Court found that the population disparity in West Virginia's apportionment of voting districts did not violate Article I Section 2 of the U.S. Constitution.

name: Minneci v. Pollard
question: Can employees of private prison operators be sued for violating the constitutional rights of inmates?
description: A case in which the Court held that a prisoner cannot assert an Eighth Amendment claim for damages against private prison employees.

name: American Tradition Partnership, Inc. v. Bullock
question: Does the Montana state law violate the First Amendment rights of corporations?
description: A case in which the Court held that a Montana law prohibiting corporations from giving political candidates monetary donations violated the corporations' First Amendment rights.

name: Match-E-Be-Nash-She-Wish Band v. Patchak
question:
1. Does Patchak lack standing because he does not fall within the zone-of-interests protected by the Indian Reorganization Act?

2. Is Patchak's suit precluded by sovereign immunity to quiet title claims drawn from the Quiet Title Act?
description: A case in which the Court held that a neighbor of a proposed Indian casino had standing to sue the government for taking 147 acres of a town's land under Section 465 of the Indian Reorganization Act.

name: Williams v. Illinois
question: Can an expert witness be called as a stand-in for a lab analyst who actually did a test on criminal evidence, but did not appear at the trial?
description: A case in which the Court held that testimony of an expert witness that is based on a test an expert did not personally perform is admissible and does not violate a defendant's Sixth Amendment Confrontation Clause rights.

name: Douglas v. Independent Living Center of Southern California
question: Does federal law preempt state reductions in Medicaid payments?
description: A case which the Court remanded to the Ninth Circuit regarding whether or not federal law preempts state reductions in Medicaid payments.

name: Perry v. New Hampshire
question: Do the Due Process protections against unreliable identification evidence apply to all identifications made under suggestive circumstances?
description: A case in which the Court held that the Due Process Clause does not require a preliminary inquiry into the reliability of an eyewitness' identification unless the ID was brought about under unnecessarily suggestive circumstances.

name: Mohamad v. Palestinian Authority
question: Does the Torture Victim Protection Act, 28 U.S.C. § 1350, permit actions against defendants who are not natural persons?
description: A case in which the Court held that the word "individual" in the Torture Victim Protection Act means a natural person and does not impose any liability against organizations.

name: Mims v. Arrow Financial Services, LLC
question: Did Congress divest the federal district courts of their federal-question jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1331 over private actions brought under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act?
description: A case in which the Court held that the Telephone Consumer Protection Act does not strip federal courts of the ability to hear cases that would normally be brought in state courts.

name: Hardy v. Cross
question: Did the steps taken to attempt to locate A.S. satisfy the Confrontation Clause's good faith effort requirement?
description: A case in which the Court held that the Confrontation Clause does not require the State to exhaust every possible avenue, even highly unlikely ones, in attempts to obtain witnesses to testify for trial.

name: Reichle v. Howards
question:
1. Does probable cause to make an arrest bar a First Amendment retaliatory arrest claim?

2. Do Secret Service agents have qualified immunity in the matter of an arrest for which there was probable cause consistent with the Fourth Amendment?
description: A case in which the Court held that police officers and federal agents cannot be sued for violating someone’s rights, as long as the right that was supposedly violated was not formally recognized to exist at the time the officers acted.

name: Wetzel v. Lambert
question: Did the Third Circuit properly apply the habeas deference standard to the state courts' rejection of Lambert's claim?
description: A case in which the Court held that courts should not grant habeas relief under the Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act of 1996 unless grounds supporting the state court decision are examined and found to be unreasonable under AEDPA.

name: Florence v. Board of Chosen Freeholders of the County of Burlington
question: Does the Fourth Amendment permit a jail to conduct a suspicion-less strip search whenever an individual is arrested, including for minor offenses?
description: A case in which the Court held that prisons that conduct suspicion-less strip searches on incoming inmates do not violate the prisoner's Fourth Amendment rights.

name: Bobby v. Dixon
question:
Did the Toledo police violate Dixon's constitutional rights by failing to read his Miranda rights during the forgery questioning?

Did the police violate the constitution by delaying the reading of Dixon's Miranda rights until the second session of his interrogation for murder?

Were Dixon's relevant confessions and statements voluntary?
description: A case in which the Court held that a man was not in custody while answering police questions, and thus did not have his Miranda rights violated when they were not recited to him.

name: Wood v. Milyard
question:
1) Does an appellate court have the authority to raise the statute of limitations defense without a request by any party?

2) Does the state's declaration before the district court that it "will not challenge, but [is] not conceding, the timeliness of Wood's habeas petition," amount to a deliberate waiver of any statute of limitations defense the state may have had?
description: A case in which the Court held that, under Day v. McDonough, appellate courts have the authority, though not the obligation, to raise a forfeited statute of limitations defense on its own.

name: Martel v. Clair
question: Is a condemned state prisoner in federal habeas corpus proceedings entitled to replace his court-appointed counsel with another court-appointed lawyer because he expresses dissatisfaction and alleges that his counsel was failing to pursue potentially important evidence?
description: A case in which the Court held that a condemned state prisoner in federal proceedings is not entitled to replace his court-appointed counsel with another court-appointed counsel due to dissatisfaction with the counsel's service.

name: Parker v. Matthews
question:
1. Did the Sixth Circuit err in rejecting the Kentucky Supreme Court's interpretation of extreme emotional disturbance in Kentucky's murder statute?

2. Did the Sixth Circuit err by rejecting the Kentucky Supreme Court's finding of sufficient evidence to support two murder convictions in light of the factual findings?

3. Did the Sixth Circuit err by concluding that the prosecutor's guilt-phase closing argument violated the Due Process Clause and by rejecting the Kentucky Supreme Court's ruling?
description: A case in which the Court found that the Sixth Circuit improperly used its own precedent in deciding an appeal from a murder conviction, and that circuit precedent does not constitute clearly established federal law, so it cannot form the basis for habeas relief.

name: Roberts v. Sea-Land Services
question: Under the Longshore Act, is the period when an individual is newly awarded compensation the fiscal year when an injured worker first becomes entitled to compensation or the fiscal year when the injured worker is actually awarded compensation?
description: A case in which the Court held that the Longshore Act sets the period when an injured worker is awarded disability compensation as the fiscal year when the worker first becomes entitled to compensation.

name: Southern Union Company v. United States
question: In light of the rights to criminal due process under the Fifth Amendment and a trial by jury under the Sixth Amendment, must a fact that increases the penalty for a crime, beyond the prescribed statutory maximum, be submitted to a jury and proved beyond a reasonable doubt if the penalty is the imposition of criminal fines?
description: A case in which the Court held that the rule applied in Apprendi v. New Jersey, where the Sixth Amendment’s guarantee of a jury trial requires that any fact which increases the maximum punishment for a particular crime be proved to a jury, applies to the imposition of criminal fines.

name: Arizona v. United States
question: Do the federal immigration laws preclude Arizona's efforts at cooperative law enforcement and preempt the four provisions of S.B. 1070 on their face?
description: A case in which the Court found that Arizona's state immigration provisions conflicted in part with federal immigration laws.

name: Kurns v. Railroad Friction Products Corp.
question: Did Congress intend the federal railroad safety acts to preempt state-law-based tort lawsuits?
description: A case in which the Court held that the Locomotive Inspection Act preempts state law design defect claims and state law failure to warn claims.

name: Holder v. Gutierrez
question:
1. Can a parent's years of lawful permanent resident status be applied to an alien who resided with that parent as an unemancipated minor, for the purpose of satisfying 8 U.S.C. 1229b(a)(1)'s requirement that the alien seeking cancellation of removal have "been an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence for not less than 5 years"?

2. Can a parent's years of residence after lawful admission to the United States can be applied to an alien who resided with that parent as an unemancipated minor, for the purpose of satisfying 8 U.S.C. 1229b(a)(2)'s requirement that the alien seeking cancellation of removal have "resided in the United States continuously for 7 years after having been admitted in any status"?
description: A case in which the Court held that an unemancipated minor cannot use his or her parent's years of residency to fulfill the requirements for having a removal from the country stayed under 8 U.S. C. 1229(a).

name: Magner v. Gallagher
question: Are disparate impact claims permitted under the Fair Housing Act?
description: A case which was dismissed regarding whether or not disparate impact claims are permitted under the Fair Housing Act.

name: Miller v. Alabama
question: Does the imposition of a life-without-parole sentence on a fourteen-year-old child violate the Eighth and Fourteenth Amendments' prohibition against cruel and unusual punishment?
description: A case in which the Court found it to be a violation of the Eighth Amendment to impose a sentence of life imprisonment without the possibility of parole on juvenile offenders.

name: Kappos v. Hyatt
question:
(1) Can a plaintiff, who is appealing the denial of an application of a patent by commencing a civil action against the Director of the United States Patent and Trademark Office (PTO) in a federal district court pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 145, introduce new evidence that could have been presented to the agency in the first instance?

(2) When new evidence is introduced under Section 145, can the district court decide de novo the factual questions to which the evidence pertains, without giving deference to the prior decision of the PTO?
description: A case in which the Court held that a patent applicant's ability to introduce new evidence in a civil action against the Patent and Trademark Office was only limited by the Federal Rules of Evidence and the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure.

name: Knox v. Service Employees International Union
question:
(1) May a State, consistent with the First and Fourteenth Amendments, condition employment on the payment of a special union assessment intended solely for political and ideological expenditures without first providing a notice that includes information about that assessment and provides an opportunity to object to its exaction?

(2) May a State, consistent with the First and Fourteenth Amendments, condition continued public employment on the payment of union agency fees for purposes of financing political expenditures for ballot measures?
description: A case in which the Court found that, under the First Amendment, public-sector unions are not permitted to impose a special assessment fee without the consent of the member upon whom it is imposed.

name: Golan v. Holder
question:
(1) Does the Progress Clause of the U.S. Constitution prohibit Congress from taking works out of the public domain?

(2) Does Section 514 of the Uruguay Round Agreements Act violate the First Amendment of the United States Constitution?
description: A case in which the Court held that Section 514 of the Uruguay Round Agreements Act, regarding copyright status of works in the public domain, does not violate the Copyright Clause or the First Amendment.

name: Filarsky v. Delia
question: If a private lawyer is retained by the government, is that attorney precluded from claiming qualified immunity solely because he or she is a private lawyer rather than a government employee?
description: A case in which the Court found that a private attorney retained by a governmental agency is not prevented from claiming qualified immunity simply because they are not a full-time employee of the agency.

name: Kiobel v. Royal Dutch Petroleum
question:
1. Under the Alien Tort Statute, are corporations immune from tort liability for violations of the law of nations, such as torture, extrajudicial executions, or genocide?

2. Upon reargument, does the Alien Tort Statute allow courts to recognize a cause of action for violations of the law of nations occurring within the territory of a sovereign other than the United States?
description: A case in which the Court found that the Alien Tort Statute does not give ground for United States law to be applied extraterrestrially to other sovereign nations with their own laws.

name: Judulang v. Holder
question: Can a lawful permanent resident who was convicted by guilty plea of an offense that renders him deportable and excludable under differently phrased statutory subsections be prevented from seeking discretionary relief from removal under former Section 212(c) of the Immigration and Nationality Act?
